Jamo is one of a kind. Only he can front flip into the end zone one week after Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL celebrating with a jump. The good news is not that he landed it (he didn't); it's that he keeps finding the end zone. He's the WR20 on WR34 usage this season now. Jared Goff is dynamite right now and was able to hang in the pocket to deliver a strike to Jamo on his post TD. He's only averaging 3.6 receptions per game this year, but he certainly makes them count as usual.

This matchup is a dreamy one. The Bears have been nuked on double moves and go balls by outside speed receivers this year. They've allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs on 15+ air-yard throws, while limiting underneath receivers with slot CB Kyler Gordon (questionable) as their top corner. Williams has been the WR20, WR10 and WR4 in his most recent games against them. The Lions are a rare underdog here, yet still have a 26.5-point team total (fifth) in what is obviously a potential shoutout.

Burden is going to be very volatile in this role. He only played 12 of 27 snaps with multiple TEs on the field, playing behind Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond. The Bears love his YAC ability but don't trust him in all ways at the moment. That's part of the reason why he's an All-Pro in first halves and goes away in second halves. Burden is the WR21 on WR42 usage in games with Caleb Williams this season on a team-high 22% target share.

The Lions won't have DE1 and LB1, and they have already been averaging 254 passing YPG (fourth most) as a pass funnel. A team total of 29.0 points (third) with the division on the line are the cherries on top.

Moore had the best breaking-route tape of his season just last week, ultimately scoring a red-zone touchdown on the backside of a Josh Allen progression. A 23% target share on a great offense is a great place to be with his YAC ability. He had a season-high 17.0 expected half PPR points last week.

19. Zay Flowers (at HOU) - 67.5 proj. receiving yards

20. Drake London (at MIN) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

21. DeVonta Smith (at DAL) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

The good news is he looked healthy, and the defense is in a bad spot, so there will be game script on his side often.

The matchup with the Cowboys is a bit more challenging with CB1 Joey Porter Jr. healthy again, but they have been hilariously bad all year for a million reasons. And still, the Eagles have a 19.5-point team total (23rd).

23. Tetairoa McMillan (at TB) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

24. Denzel Boston (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

25. Rome Odunze (at DET) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Odunze is the WR33 on WR42 usage since Week 6 when Caleb Williams returned. He's not getting the volume of a must-start WR3, but Odunze is a downfield and red-zone threat in an awesome offense. If he can secure the ball cleanly, there will be a massive game from him down the stretch here.

This unit has allowed the 11th-most fantasy points to WRs on 15+ air yard targets, and that will be a lot easier with a backup corner on Odunze. Back in Week 2 of last year, Odunze had 128 yards and two scores against this defense. That was his best game in terms of targets (11), receptions (seven) and fantasy points (28.3 half PPR). The Bears enter as 2.5-point road favorites with a 29-point team total (third).

27. Rashee Rice (at BUF) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Rice isn't going to reach his top-10 fantasy WR status in this new role, but he's held the line as a fantasy WR2/3. Over the past month since his injury, Rice is the WR28 on WR36 usage with Josh Downs now involved on similar intermediate routes. He's had a 20% target share this month with a 5.6 aDOT. The Chiefs opted for a WR-by-committee last week to make sure Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong got snaps, too. Rice played 22-of-39 receiving snaps (56%) through three quarters. We'll see if he keeps getting the occasional deep target as he's had recently. That'd be his best way to add the occasional spike week.

The Bills are weakest through the air, though new S1 Amani Hooker is going to shore things up moving forward. They've allowed the 14th-most fantasy points to WRs this year and CB1 Christian Benford hasn't played recently. If he can't go, there is a clear opportunity for all WRs. Rice had 86-1 against Buffalo last year for what it's worth. The Chiefs enter Thanksgiving as 3-point road underdogs with an implied total of 23.75 points (11th).

28. KC Concepcion (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

29. Carnell Tate (at JAX) - 44.5 proj. receiving yards

30. DeMario Douglas (at LAC) - 25.5 proj. receiving yards

31. Caleb Douglas (vs. NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

32. Khalil Shakir (vs. KC) - 42.5 proj. receiving yards

#2686. Why Kim Caldwell is optimistic about Tennessee after loss to UCLA

KNOXVILLE, TN — Kim Caldwell, Kaylene Smikle and Fatmata Janneh walked into the postgame press conference in an upbeat mood and with their heads held high. It was easy to hear Janneh cutting up and laughing in the hallway before they walked in.

The Tennessee Lady Vols weren't carrying the demeanor of a team that had just suffered its first loss of the season, 90-80 to No. 10 UCLA on Sunday, Nov. 22. Caldwell and her players felt optimistic.

Obviously, they wanted to win, but Caldwell liked some of the things she saw. She witnessed a brand new roster play her system and style against a marquee opponent. She saw them compete hard on the court with the reigning national champions.

"I hate the result of that game. I hate to lose. I think that we could have won that game," Caldwell said. "I think there's a lot of room for improvement with this team. There's a lot of things that we practiced and we prepped for that we didn't do correctly. There's a lot of things we needed to adjust to on the fly.

"But I think everyone in our locker room knows we can get 10 to 12 points better. We are confident moving forward that we have a team that is bought in. We'll fix those things, they want to fix those things, and hopefully by the time March rolls around and we see a team of that caliber, we're much improved."

Caldwell is in her third season now as the head coach of the storied program in Knoxville that won eight national championships under the legendary Pat Summitt. Nearly two decades have passed since Tennessee has been to a Final Four and it's been more than 10 years since they appeared in the Elite Eight.

Tennessee exceeded expectations in Caldwell's first season, defeating UConn in the regular season and then advancing to the Sweet 16. But last year was the worst single-season campaign in program history as the Lady Vols ended the year on an eight-game losing streak and limped to a 16-14 record.

In the offseason, the entire roster flipped over and changes were made to the coaching staff. Caldwell brought in 13 transfers, players she believed would commit to her up-tempo, pressing scheme, and ones who would be unbothered by her frequent hockey-style substitution patterns. The Lady Vols started this season 6-0 and pushed UCLA into some uncomfortable situations.

For Bruins' head coach Cori Close, this Tennessee team is much better than the ones the Bruins beat in Los Angeles last year.

"If you look at how they're playing together and their chemistry and how they're executing what Coach Kim really wants them to do, I thought they might have been playing better collectively (than last season)," Close said. "They're still growing together as well. But I thought they might be playing closer to the identity that their staff is trying to develop. (Caldwell) gives you all you can handle because their style of play is so unusual. It really takes the power out of my hands. I feel very hopeless most of the game."

Aside from seeming to have a collective unit that is committed to the way that Caldwell wants to play, what else has emerged for Tennessee across their first seven games is that they have a clear on-court leader in Kaylene Smikle. The Maryland transfer missed most of last season with a knee injury, but seems to be regaining the form that earned her two All-Big Ten nods.

Smikle finished with 27 points and 10 rebounds against UCLA, notching just the third double-double of her career. The 6-foot, fifth-year guard from New York is averaging 22 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.6 steals per game while shooting 52.9% from the floor — all career-high marks.

"The thing about her is she just has a will to win. And it's not even to score — we obviously see that she can score the ball, but a will to make the right play, a will to get the ball back, a will to rip down four offensive rebounds, and that's who she is as a player," Caldwell said of Smikle. "And I think as she continues with us, you're going to see her get better and better on both sides of the ball. You're going to see her become a better leader. You're going to see her start to call huddles and bring people with her because she plays with a sense of urgency."

Asked about what positives she took away from the result against the Bruins, Smikle said, "We didn't give up, not one time."

That's the sort of fight and attitude Caldwell wants her teams to show. It's a stark contrast from last season when Caldwell said her team had "a lot of quit" in them following a lopsided loss to South Carolina. But those players are gone. This is a brand new team, handpicked by Caldwell.

"What I wanted when I constructed this roster was a lot of players that wanted to play this way, that have the same underdog, chip-on-their-shoulder mentality that I do," Caldwell said. "It's about winning. It's about making the right play. When you can have 15 people that it's about winning, then I think the sky is the limit."

Caldwell is still learning what kind of team she has. It remains to be seen whether they will have what it takes to compete at the top of the SEC. But what's clear three weeks into the season is that this group of Lady Vols are fighters. It's a group that Caldwell is confident with going into every game.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why Kim Caldwell is optimistic about Tennessee after loss to UCLA

#2682. JJ Redick reveals rarely-seen qualities that separate this Lakers team

One of the reasons why things are clicking so seamlessly?

Apparently none of the team's wings are keeping score of petty things, such as who starts, who gets more touches, etc.

Lakers coach JJ Redick has a theory as to why that's happening.

"I think they're all really grateful to be here, to be Lakers," Redick said after the Lakers' 109-94 win over the Jazz on Monday. "They're all really grateful to be on this team and be part of the group."

Redick pointed out that Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes and Jake LaRavia are all in the same boat even though different circumstances brought them to this moment.

In other words, they all know this is a rare opportunity.

They deeply understand that playing for a Laker team that is tied for the best record in the league at 15-3 and has a real shot at winning a championship is something worth sacrificing for.

"They've experienced adversity in their careers, in different ways, and I think that gratitude piece is like they're all in a situation [together]," Redick said. "…They're just all in a situation where they're putting the team first and they're putting their egos aside and that stuff matters and I think you know it's one of the reasons our group has had early success because we said on day one we wanted this season to be about the team and not any one individual one of us, and so far it's been that."

Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick looks on before an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images

Jake LaRavia started in 11 straight games before coming off the bench in the team's two contests prior to their win over the Jazz. He returned to the starting lineup Monday, finishing with 15 points, 10 rebounds and two steals.

"I've talked about it before, I think just everyone is willing to sacrifice for the same goal, and we just have a lot of adaptable players," LaRavia said.

"A lot of it's like lineup-based, matchup-based, so you know, whoever the coaches think should start that night is who's going to start. And I think as players we're all willing to be kind of thrown in and out of the lineup.

"And it doesn't really change much for us as players. You just, you know, keep the same mindset and keep the same goal and just go out there and play hard."

Jake LaRavia (12) of the Los Angeles Lakers dribbles during a game against the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images

As for Redick, he said this roster lends itself to experimenting with different rotations, as he did by putting Ziaire Williams in the starting lineup for LaRavia in a loss against the Jazz on Nov. 18 and a win over the Kings on Nov. 20.

"This group is like malleable to lineup changes, you know, tweaking rotations," Redick said. "They understand that we're still trying to figure out the group and what's best for the group. So I don't think [Ziaire] or Jake was affected at all by you know the two games with Z in the starting lineup. And we were really good with Jake in the starting lineup. We were going to go back to it at some point. We went back to it [Monday], and he played a great game."

Keyonte George #3 of the Utah Jazz drives against Ziaire Williams #11 of the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images

The Lakers have won 11 of their last 12 games, including five of their last victories coming while Austin Reaves has been sidelined because of a left heel bruise.

Things are clicking. The chemistry is great. The locker room has good vibes.

And everyone seemingly is focused on the bigger picture instead of individual accolades or perceived slights.

"At the end of the day, we have a lot of guys who haven't been able to give it their all to win, and whenever we're able to, I feel like we're going to give it our heart and give it our all," Collin Sexton said.

"And I feel like [general manager] Rob [Pelinka] did a great job of bringing guys in that's ready to be selfless, but also ready to do whatever needed to win, and play whatever role that is. So, I think when you have a locker room full of guys who want to win more than themself, and no one cares about who's the hero at the end of the day, it's like we're going to give it our all."

#2677. Three Vols named finalists for prestigious individual awards

The Tennessee Vols have been elite in 2026 on defense and in the running game, both of which have powered the program to the edge of their second College Football Playoff berth in three years.

And on Tuesday, three crucial parts of those two aspects were appropriately recognized for their efforts.

DeSean Bishop, Xavier Gilliam, and Jim Knowles were all named finalists for their respective national awards in their respective positions/role.

Bishop will be interesting for the Doak Walker Award. Iowa State's Aiden Flora (1506 rushing yards, 14 rushing TDs) and Duke's Nate Sheppard (1436; 20) both lead Bishop (1215; 13) by a decent margin in the two key rushing categories. Bishop is tied for 10th nationally in rushing yards. But no player has arguably been as important to a college football playoff contender this year than Bishop has been for Tennessee. He's carried the Vols on his back offensively and powered them through quarterback injuries and inexperience to tough four-quarter wins this year. That's clearly mattered. After not even being on the preseason watch list, he's not a finalist. Quite the rise.

Gilliam has been a one-man wrecking ball in the middle of the Vols' defense. He has shattered career marks with 28 total tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss, and seven sacks. He's getting plenty of first round draft buzz, and we're not talking in the back end. He's got top 10 potential and could become one of the highest drafted Tennessee players in a very long time (OT Darnell Wright was first player since Eric Berry in 2010 to be drafted in the top 10 back in 2023).

Knowles has proven himself to be an ingenious hire by Josh Heupel this past offseason. With so many new faces via the portal and no established edge rushers in place coming into the season, there were plenty of question marks. But Knowles' group has proven to be one of the most physical and productive defenses in the nation and served as a foundation for Tennessee's success this year.

Without a doubt, all three finalists are well deserved. Best of luck to the trio.

#2671. Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers: Now what?

Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Tuesday cleared waivers after being let go by the team Monday according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Because Aiyuk was released after the trade deadline he was subject to waivers. The claiming team would've had to take on his contract which helps explain why a club wasn't willing to take a flyer on him via the waiver system.

By clearing waivers Aiyuk is now an unrestricted free agent. He's available to sign with any team that will give him a contract.

San Francisco was given a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk after he was reinstated to the NFL on Nov. 9. Had the 49ers not waived Aiyuk on Monday they would've had to release a player to clear a roster spot for the disgruntled wide receiver.

Whether Aiyuk gets a contract offer from another NFL team remains to be seen. There was a heavy social media flirtation with the Washington Commanders by Aiyuk during his NFL hiatus. Aiyuk is also familiar with Commanders general manager Adam Peters who was in the 49ers' front office when Aiyuk was selected by San Francisco in the first round of the 2020 draft. It's unclear whether teams will be willing to take a risk on the former All-Pro after his tumultuous exit from San Francisco.

Aiyuk hasn't played since injuring his knee in Week 7 of the 2024 season. He didn't return for the 2025 campaign and during that time the relationship between the receiver and the 49ers fractured, leading to him being placed on the reserve/left squad list last season and remaining there until his reinstatement in early November of this year.

When Aiyuk was healthy he was growing toward becoming one of the NFL's top pass catchers. In 2023 he earned a second-team All-Pro nod when he caught 75 balls for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. His numbers were on track to dip some as he struggled out of the gate in 2024 following a long training camp holdout while negotiating a long-term contract. In 2024 before his injury he had 25 catches for 374 yards.

In five seasons with the 49ers Aiyuk played in 70 games with 67 starts. He caught 294 passes for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns. He added 13 carries for 117 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.

#2670. Highlights: Spurs rule once again on the road against the Kings

The San Antonio Spurs kept the show rolling on the road for their 8th win. This time, the boys in Black and White notched a win without starters such as Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, and Dylan Harper. Stephon Castle led the way with 28 points, 11 assists, and 8 rebounds. Julian Champagnie and Luke Kornet also played a huge role in the win without 22 points and 18 points scored, respectively. Kornet slotted in seamlessly and controlled the glass to the tune of 11 rebounds to achieve a double-double.

Jordan McLaughlin likes his turkey dry, but he provided plenty of sauce on this move to the bucket. The wily veteran guard (and former Sacramento King) stepped up for the short-staffed Spurs and contributed 6 points and 2 rebounds in 14 minutes of solid play.

Speaking of White Castle, they are opening up a White Castle (burger restaurant) in the DFW area, which is the only good thing about living up here as a Spurs fan away from my P. Terry's and Hawx Burger Bar (R.I.P.). I know P.Terry's is more Austin than San Antonio, but sometimes you want something like In 'N Out, but slightly less California-y and more Austin-y even though they're both the same type of burgers and fries with a small menu and similar vibe. If you don't agree, that's your right to do so, but it doesn't bring back my beloved Hawx Burger Bar.

I usually do not post highlights of three-pointers (unless they are really, really extraordinary like full-court shots or Victor Wembanyama bouncing one off the backboard before he takes a three (he WILL attempt this before it's all said and done)) because dunking and Euro-stepping through a sea of 7-foot-wing-spanned arms seems more extraordinary. That being said, I want to take a moment to appreciate Spurs rookie Ja'Kobi Gillispie's pretty shot from downtown. His shot was so pretty, I want to name it "Lucia" and dote on it like apparently one does on Grand Theft Auto VI.

Keldon Johnson flicked his wrist for this prompt alley-oop to Luke Kornet. Kornet, filling in for Victor Wembanyama, had a superb box score of 18 points and 11 rebounds. Perhaps just having extra minutes to get some burn is exactly what Kornet needs to get into a groove as the season wears on. The team and Spurs fans would certainly love to see the big man provide some punch from the bench, especially to give Wembanyama a breather either in minutes or entire games.

Watch closely below at that subtle move Kornet makes when he fakes a pass and then blows by his defender for the jam. That's exactly what you have to do with the Thanksgiving sides when you want to take more than your share after someone passes you the dish: you gotta fake passing it to the next person and dump the entire contents of smoked cabbage (w/bacon) onto your plate. If your daughter starts crying, the wife begins to contemplate divorce, and the dog looks at you with shame, well you just think of how Luke Kornet shook off his defender and you remind yourself that winning takes sacrifice.

Kornet off another alley-oop, once again reminding us that Thanksgiving mac and cheese is not Thanksgiving mac and cheese if you don't use smoked gouda cheese with sharp cheddar. Also, fried or smoked turkey is the preferred method if you have the setup.

Happy Thanksgiving, fellow Pounders! May your gravy boat flow over with gratitude and blessings.

#2666. Prime Joel Embiid is a thing of the past, and that’s OK for the Sixers

For a grand majority of Joel Embiid's tenure in Philadelphia, the Sixers have only gone as far as he dragged them. His on/off splits are the stuff of legend, particularly in the playoffs.

But as his injuries piled up in recent years, the Sixers began the process of pivoting away from him as their focal point. Tyrese Maxey, whom Embiid nicknamed "The Franchise" a few years ago, started to live up to that promise following the departure of James Harden.

The additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown this offseason led to an onslaught of questions about "alphas" and whether the Sixers could share the ball well enough to keep all of their stars happy. One 14-4 start later, their vibes are immaculate for now.

However, one rival scout doesn't believe it'll last.

"I think it's going to be a problem, and that could railroad them," the scout told ESPN's Tim MacMahon in reference to Embiid taking more of a backseat on offense this season. "I just don't buy it right now. He's going to want the ball more. He's going to get pissed. He's going to stop playing defense. He's going to stop running."

Thus far, the exact opposite has played out.

Through his first 14 games this season, Embiid is averaging only 20.4 per outing while shooting a career-worst 40.0 percent overall and 14.3 percent from deep. That hasn't caused him to check out on defense, though. Instead, he's averaging 8.9 rebounds per game—his most since the 2023-24 campaign—and he's looking more spry defensively than he has in years.

After the Sixers' season-opening win over the New York Knicks, Embiid told reporters that he planned to vie for a spot on the All-Defense teams like he did earlier in his career because "that changes everything for our team."

That is the exact right mentality for Embiid to have this season.

For years, he's quietly bemoaned the lack of offensive support that he's had around him. Yes, the likes of Harden, Paul George, Jimmy Butler and Ben Simmons have all cycled through Philadelphia over the past decade, but more often than not, the Sixers were drawing dead without a big game from the big fella. This year is the first time where that isn't the case on a night-to-night basis.

Look no further than their NBA Cup win over the reigning-Cup-champion Knicks. Embiid finished with 10 points on 3-of-12 shooting. Prior to that game, he had finished with 10 or fewer points only 15 times across his career, many of which he left early because of injuries. (Somewhat surprisingly, the Sixers went 7-8 in those games.)

Despite his cold-shooting night, Embiid found other ways to make an impact against the Knicks. He finished with seven rebounds, seven assists (trailing only LeBron James' eight dimes on the night), one steal and one block in 33 minutes. He was a plus-eight on the game, which was tied with LeBron for the best mark among the Sixers' starters.

Embiid already had a triple-double in the third game of the season, and he nearly notched another one against the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Instead, he wound up settling for a 26-17-9 night. Ho hum.

Heading into the season, it was fair to wonder whether Embiid would be willing to take a step back on offense to focus on traditional big-man tasks such as rebounding, rim protection and screening. It was also unclear whether he still had the lateral agility to switch out on the perimeter without getting roasted alive. If not, would the Sixers be forced to keep him in drop coverage? What other tactical adjustments would they have to make to account for that?

It's still far too early in the season to take a full victory lap, but so far, so good on that front. Better yet, we're still a ways away from seeing this group's ceiling on offense as they continue to work on developing chemistry with one another.

"I think we've got a long way to go offensively," Embiid told reporters after the Sixers' win over the Chicago Bulls in early November. "A lot of it is efficiency, starting with me. A lot of guys have picked up, so it's up to me to kind of pick it up."

Embiid added that the Sixers were "on the right path" because they have the "right mentality, making plays for each other." He followed up with some revealing comments about why he might be struggling with his efficiency in the early going.

"For me, it's a little bit of an adjustment," he said. "I'm such a rhythm guy. Over the years, obviously I've had a lot of opportunities to just touch the ball almost every other possession. Sometimes you can just go four or five possessions where you don't touch the ball. That's where it's kind of like an adjustment. I'm not used to catch-and-shoot as much, I'm used to more creating for myself. So I'm working on that."

But lest that anonymous scout who spoke with MacMahon feel the need to start crowing about his prophecy, Embiid quickly shot down the notion that he'd allow his own offensive struggles to impact the rest of his game.

"My mindset is really whenever I have the ball, make plays," he said. "Make the game easy for all these guys. Making the right plays over and over. Setting screens. Get Tyrese as open as much as possible. Bron. All these guys. Just kind of being the hub and trying to get these guys open and make plays for them. That's really what the focus is on.

"And then on the other side, also, working on myself. How can I get back to that level of dominance without having as much touches as I'm used to? That's a work in progress. That's where really the struggle has been because, like I said, I'm a rhythm guy. I need to feel the ball. I need to touch the ball. When you don't, it's a little different. But it's a fun process, and I'm enjoying it, trying to find ways to get over the hump. But I feel like once I do and I figure it out and I can really be dominant, then the sky's the limit for us."

The version of Embiid who averages 30-plus points per game might be gone for good, particularly with this compilation of talent around him. That's completely OK. In fact, that's the point of assembling this level of talent around him.

There will still be some nights where Embiid has it going and the Sixers need him to bully an overmatched big man in the post and/or draw a parade of trips to the free-throw line. Against the Detroit Pistons in early November, he dominated poor BBall Paul and finished with 26 points and a season-high 15 rebounds. As Liberty Ballers' own Paul Hudrick noted, he hadn't pulled down that many boards in regulation of a regular-season game in almost three years.

The Sixers will need Embiid's threes to start dropping at some point just to keep defenses honest. But they no longer need him to be the MVP version of himself on a night-in, night-out basis. Maxey, LeBron, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe are here to shoulder some of that offensive burden, not to mention snipers like Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope off the bench.

Individually, Embiid has already done everything that he could have dreamed of accomplishing in the NBA. An MVP award, five All-NBA nods and seven All-Star selections later, the only thing left to do is win it all.

As long as he remains committed to focusing on the role that the Sixers need him to play this year, he'll have his best shot yet of doing so.

#2665. From sixth-round pick to starter: Inside Logan Taylor’s rise with Chargers

When the Chargers selected offensive lineman Logan Taylor in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, the thought was that they were just adding versatile depth in the trenches. No one penciled the former Boston College product as a starter in his rookie season.

Yet, after a wave of early-season injuries sidelined key veterans, Taylor was thrust into the fire, and he hasn't given the job back.

It began in Week 4 against the Seahawks. After Trevor Penning went down, Taylor stepped in at left guard, then moved to left tackle late in the fourth quarter after Rashawn Slater got hurt. While his emergency snaps at tackle came with growing pains, sliding back inside to his natural guard spot sparked an immediate turnaround.

With 46 collegiate starts across four positions at Virginia and Boston College, Taylor quickly adjusted to NFL speed. Playing alongside left tackle Joe Alt, the Canadian native has brought stability to a position that had operated like a revolving door.

Entering Week 11, Taylor had logged 343 snaps at guard without committing a single penalty and allowed just seven total pressures across his first 354 offensive snaps.

In the Chargers' primetime victory over the Ravens, Taylor allowed no pressures and helped set up running back Omarion Hampton's breakout rushing performance.

Most recently, in the loss to the Jets, Taylor delivered his highest-graded performance of the season. According to Pro Football Focus, Taylor finished as Los Angeles' top-graded offensive lineman overall (78.9), posting a team-best 77.6 run-blocking grade alongside a 69.2 mark in pass protection.

The validation of Taylor's play arrived ahead of the game against New York when original starter Kayode Awosika returned from injury. Rather than resorting to Awosika, head coach Jim Harbaugh confirmed that Taylor officially earned the right to remain the starter.

What began as an emergency injury replacement has quickly become a big late-round steal in the 2026 draft class. If Taylor continues to build on his midseason momentum, the Chargers may have found their long-term answer at left guard for the foreseeable future.

#2664. Dan Quinn: Scars from our late-game losses run deep, glad Jayden Daniels won it for us

The Commanders have repeatedly come up short this season in the final seconds of close games. Commanders coach Dan Quinn acknowledged that was motivating him to get it right in the final seconds of Monday night’s win over the Bengals.

“Those scars run deep,” Quinn said. “There’s no question, failures in some. And I think those scars help.”

“I couldn’t have been more proud of Jayden at the end of the game,” Quinn said. “To see those guys come through at the end, I thought that was one of our best team wins. I didn’t think anything could top last week’s but tonight did.”

The Commanders are now 4-5-1 and still alive in the NFC East race. And they have some confidence that if they need their quarterback to deliver in the clutch, he’ll deliver.

#2663. Observations after Sixers' 5-game win streak ends with blowout loss to Blazers

Observations after Sixers' 5-game win streak ends with blowout loss to Blazers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers' five-game winning streak was snapped Monday night by the Trail Blazers.

With a 128-111 defeat at Xfinity Mobile Arena, the Sixers dropped their first game of the year against Western Conference opposition and fell to 14-4. Portland improved to 11-6.

LeBron James had a season-high 23 points and six rebounds. Tyrese Maxey scored 22 points and Jaylen Brown added 20.

Deni Avdija led the Blazers with 31 points and seven assists. Donovan Clingan posted 15 points and 18 rebounds.

The Sixers were missing Joel Embiid (illness). Ja Morant (left hamstring strain) and Shaedon Sharpe (right knee meniscus surgery) were among Portland's sidelined players.

Next on the Sixers' schedule is a Wednesday night game vs. the Heat. Here are observations on their blowout loss to the Blazers:

Jabari Walker, listed at 6-foot-7, defied conventional wisdom by winning the opening tip-off against the 7-2 Cllingan. Maxey then canned a three-pointer.

Brown scored the Sixers' next four points with a pair of free throws and a short jumper. VJ Edgecombe's layup gave the team a 9-2 lead. Brown and Dean Wade both returned Monday after sitting out the last two games with left hamstring injuries.

Avdija got hot in the first quarter. He scored 11 quick points, made his first four field goals and helped the Blazers avoid a serious early deficit.

The Sixers took a 32-30 edge with 9.3 seconds left in the first when Walker jammed in a put-back dunk. The former Portland second-round draft pick played 17 minutes in his second start of the season and continued to look deserving of a rotation spot. He posted 10 points and five rebounds.

Adem Bona was available again following an eight-game absence with a cervical spine sprain. However, Dominick Barlow checked in first to back up Walker.

Barlow had an outstanding start to his night. He scored a clever lefty push shot over Clingan and threw down a dunk in the first quarter. Barlow also made a highlight defensive play in his opening stint, defending Avdija in isolation and rejecting his layup attempt.

Bona then subbed in for Barlow with 3:23 left in the first quarter. He had a positive first possession, grabbing an offensive rebound and driving in for a dunk.

Wade later played at center, too. Barlow logged 16 minutes and had six points. Bona recorded four points and two boards in five minutes. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse ended up using a 10-man rotation and did not play rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr. until fourth-quarter garbage time.

Overall, the Sixers' defense remained considerably worse without Embiid. The team also conceded 15 offensive rebounds, including five to Clingan.

"I think your rim protection and ability to do that with some size is always a focal point of being really good defensively," Nurse said. "And then you've got to do it a little bit by committee (with Embiid out). I thought, for the most part, I was looking at possessions where I liked our help into the paint. They were doing a good job of zinging it out.

"I didn't particularly like our (defense) back out. … There were a couple of times they missed those and still got rebounds. We were compacted in the lane with everybody because we didn't get back out, and then still giving up an offensive rebound as well. That's just playing through the possession, a little bit of energy, all that kind of stuff. … We just didn't do enough pieces well."

Brown delivered tons of efficient offense for the Sixers in the first half and sure didn't appear rusty. His layup late in the second quarter tied the game at 58-all. The five-time All-Star scored 19 first-half points on 8-for-10 shooting.

Avdija exceeded Brown's production, hitting heat-check threes, leaners through contact and just about everything he put up regardless of the defender. He tallied 25 points in the first half and shot 9 for 12 from the field.

James reached 16 points when he capped a high-scoring half by nailing a corner three. The contest was even at 69 apiece heading into halftime.

Monday's game was James' first of the season with three or more made three-pointers. The four-time MVP went 4 for 5 beyond the arc. He'd gone 10 for 46 (21.7 percent) over his first 13 games and was due for a good long-range night.

James was whistled for his third foul early in the third quarter. Brown picked up his fourth with 10:15 to go in the period, forcing him to sit for an extended stretch.

"I wasn't too happy about it. … I think that affected the game," Brown said. "It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half. I had to sit (almost) the whole third quarter. Coming back from injury, coming back from a hamstring thing, my body didn't really feel the same after that."

Brown noted postgame that he had "a little bit of soreness and stuff like that."

"I think everything will check out," he said. "The medical staff is on top of everything. Those hamstrings are tricky, so you want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe. I also don't want to miss a lot of games, so I might be out there, but I've also got to be smart. I think I played it the right way today."

Avdija stopped lighting up the Sixers in the third period, but the team still had another unimpressive defensive quarter. Portland posted 32 points in the third and built its lead to double figures in the opening minute of the fourth.

The game devolved into a blowout. An Avdija dunk put the Blazers' advantage at 22 points with 5:15 on the clock and the Sixers didn't have a miracle comeback in store.

Even with all their wins, there's no question the Sixers have been trending downward on defense over the past couple of weeks, allowing regular dribble penetration and plenty of comfortable threes.

They'll aim to raise their level on that side of the floor and expect Embiid's presence to be a major help once he's back in action.

"I think it's just mindset," Walker said. "We're capable when we want to. You need games like this every now and then just to remind you that it's not as easy as it feels sometimes. It takes effort every game.

"I think we can learn a lot from this. It's just part of the growing pains, but I'm confident we'll get back to that (early-season) level of defense. We have what it takes."

#2662. Tee Higgins touchdown highlights inconsistency of replay review

Just when we thought we were out when it comes to not knowing what a catch is, they pull us back in.

The past two days have included three examples of plays that make more confusing the question of whether a player has completed the act of catching the ball — and whether replay review was properly used to correct rulings made on the field.

It started on Sunday afternoon, when an apparent touchdown catch by Jaguars receiver Parker Washington was ruled not a catch on the field, with replay review not overturning the ruling. Even though the visual evidence seemed to provide clear and obvious proof that the ball was caught.

On Sunday night, 49ers receiver Mike Evans bobbled his way to a touchdown catch. He quite possibly didn’t get two feet in bounds after finally securing control of the ball. The play wasn’t even reviewed.

On Monday night, Bengals receiver Tee Higgins made a touchdown catch even though the ball was moving as he landed on the ground and out of bounds. There was no replay review.

The common denominator in these plays (beyond the fact that they involved potential touchdown catches) is the shadowy, uncertain replay process. As one head coach explained it to PFT on Monday (before the Bengals-Commanders game), it’s still not known who is making the decisions in New York as to what will be reviewed and what the outcome of the review will be.

It’s another reason for the NFL to embrace full transparency when it comes to replay review. We need to know who is making the decisions. We need to know their names. We need to hear their voices.

And we also need to know why — as happened in the case of the Evans and Higgins touchdowns — there was no full-blown review.

#2660. Clock operator robbed Bengals of one final play

The Bengals-Commanders game carries a small but not insignificant asterisk.

As ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk explained in the postgame show, the clock operator incorrectly ran the remaining four seconds off the clock during the game-winning field goal from Washington.

Yurk said two seconds remained when the ball hit the net. It looks more like it should have been one second.

Regardless, Yurk said the replay process can’t restore time when the next play isn’t a scrimmage play. (There’s also a rule regarding restoring time when there are fewer than two seconds left, and — with all due respect to Yurk — it appears that there was only one second when the ball hit the net.)

The bottom line is that the clock operator was slow to get to the button, and there wasn’t anything that could be done about it.

What would have happened if the Bengals had gotten one last chance? We’ll never know, because the person hired to keep track of the time handled it incorrectly.

Or, depending on that person’s rooting interests, he handled it perfectly.

#2659. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2658. Commanders, Giants and Cowboys – this team will win the NFC East

The NFC East is one of the NFL's wilder divisions. Every team has had a wild ride this season and dealt with monumental momentum shifts.

The New York Giants lead the division at 6-3-1 and have started three different quarterbacks. The Dallas Cowboys are 5-6, but their defense has been horrible all year. At Detroit, Buffalo, at Green Bay, 49ers in Mexico City.

#2652. Hammond mayor says Bears will "make a lot more money" in Indiana

Money talks. And the mayor of Hammond hopes the Bears are listening.

At a time when the Bears are trying to get Illinois to pass a law that will lay the foundation for a stadium in the state where the Bears have always played, Indiana interests aren’t giving up.

If they wanted to go to Indiana, ground would have already been broken. At some point, however, they may have no choice but to get out the shovel. Even if getting out the shovel is the thing that will finally get Illinois to view Indiana as something more than a sham.

#2649. Report: Mike LaFleur stuck with Nick Rallis as DC due to limited options in coaching cycle

When the Cardinals hired Mike LaFleur in February, he was the last head coach to start his job in this year’s NFL cycle.

#2646. NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 12's biggest games

A week after serving up one lopsided matchup after another, the NFL has cooked up a mouthwatering Thanksgiving Week feast. Which means we're dishing out a heaping platter of NFL betting trends targeting all five midweek games on the Week 12 menu.

The festivities begin with a clash of two NFC playoff hopefuls in the first Thanksgiving Eve contest. That's followed by back-to-back Thanksgiving Day battles between NFC division rivals (including one with first place on the line).

Then, just as the second slice of pumpkin pie hits your plate Thursday night, two AFC teams with a combined 16-3 record square off in Western New York. Capping the midweek football frenzy (and our Week 12 NFL betting trends report): another matchup of AFC playoff contenders, this one on Black Friday.

• The Week 12 slate kicks off Wednesday night with a pair of teams that are 6-4 SU and ATS and coming off a bye.

Green Bay entered its bye off a surprising 30-10 blowout loss to division rival Minnesota as a 2.5-point home favorite. It was just the Packers' second loss in their last seven games and also snapped a 6-0 ATS run.

Meanwhile, the Rams emerge from their week off riding a season-best four-game winning SU/ATS streak. Three of those were road victories (35-21 at Las Vegas, 20-13 at Washington and 34-6 at Arizona), with the other a 24-9 home rout of the Chargers.

• The Packers have cashed in each of their last three games as an underdog (2-1 SU).

Also, since starting the season with non-covers in road games at the Vikings (39-22 loss as a 2.5-point favorite) and Jets (20-17 win as a 3.5-point road chalk), Green Bay has gone 3-0 ATS as a visitor (2-1 SU).

The Packers haven't covered the spread in four consecutive road contests since late in the 2009 campaign.

• This is the fourth time in as many seasons in which Los Angeles has enjoyed a 4-0 ATS run.

During this time, the Rams' lengthiest point spread hot streak was five games in 2023 (Weeks 12-16). It's their only 5-0 ATS heater since early in 2003.

Another NFL betting trend worth nothing: The Rams were favored in all four games during their current 4-0 ATS surge. They haven't covered five in a row as a favorite since the 1999 Super Bowl-winning team went 7-0 ATS from Weeks 10-16.

• These teams squared off in five straight seasons from 2020-2024 (including a 2020 playoff matchup). The Packers were favored in four of the games and went 5-0 SU and ATS.

In fact, since 2007 and including the postseason clash in 2020, Green Bay is 9-1 SU and 10-0 ATS against the Rams, including 5-0 SU and ATS on the road.

• The under is 6-1 in the Packers' last seven and 3-1 in their last four on the highway. What's more, six of Green Bay's last eight overall — including three of four on the road — have fallen shy of 40 combined points.

Sixers' record-setting wait for the West ends against Trail Blazers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

When the Sixers welcome the Portland Trail Blazers to Xfinity Mobile Arena on Monday night, it will mark the latest they have ever gone into a season before facing a Western Conference team.

Philadelphia's 18-game wait also ties the 1979-80 Atlanta Hawks for the second latest by an Eastern Conference team. Only the 1980-81 Milwaukee Bucks went longer, meeting the West for the first time in their 21st game.

The Sixers have played who has been placed in front of them and won five consecutive games. They have already beaten the Knicks twice and own victories over Cleveland and Detroit.

Their first Western Conference matchup introduces a different comparison.

The West entered Monday with 11 teams above .500. The East had seven. Western Conference teams were also 41-20 against the East through Sunday.

Portland will not answer every question about how the Sixers compare with the other conference. It begins a more varied portion of their schedule.

The Sixers will face Memphis and Denver on consecutive nights next week. Dallas and Houston visit later in December before Philadelphia travels to play the Lakers, Clippers, Kings and Suns over a six-day stretch.

Portland is 10-6 under first-year head coach Micah Nori, the father of Phillies prospect Dante Nori.

The Blazers are averaging 116.1 points while allowing 110.3 per game, with both figures ranking in the top 10. Their 15.4 made three-pointers per game rank second in the NBA.

Deni Avdija leads Portland with 23.9 points per game. Damian Lillard is averaging 20.6 points in his return to the franchise, while 7-foot-2 center Donovan Clingan has supplied size around a deep group of guards and wings.

Clingan posted 22 points and 13 rebounds Saturday night at Madison Square Garden. Portland erased a 26-point deficit and briefly took the lead before Mikal Bridges made a game-winning three-pointer at the buzzer.

The 97-96 loss dropped the Blazers to 1-3 over their last four games. Slow starts have followed them during that stretch.

"Our last three games, we haven't gotten off to great starts, and that's just something that we got to correct," Lillard said. "Our energy and our focus and our intent has to be better from the jump. We can't let this trend continue."

The Sixers know something about overcoming early deficits. Six of their 14 victories have required double-digit comebacks.

Even without Morant, the Blazers can turn to Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson to initiate their offense. Avdija and Toumani Camara provide size on the perimeter, while Clingan gives Portland the kind of interior presence that has occasionally troubled the Sixers.

Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker know the Portland organization better than any other Sixers.

The two shared the floor for 128 games with the Trail Blazers. Portland won 43 of them.

Their responsibilities have changed in Philadelphia. So have the expectations.

Simons scored 18 points in each of the Sixers' last two games and made seven three-pointers. He started in place of Tyrese Maxey against Orlando and hit the clinching three in his hometown. Three nights later, he supplied four more threes off the bench in the Sixers' 132-129 win over Milwaukee.

Walker has also found steady work during the Sixers' recent frontcourt injuries. He recorded nine points, seven rebounds and four assists against the Bucks after scoring 11 against Indiana and hitting a go-ahead three late in Orlando.

Both players recently discussed how their difficult seasons in Portland changed their perspective on filling smaller roles for a winning team.

"You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you're winning," Simons said. "That's something that you can't take for granted, for sure, because it's hard to win in the NBA. We've seen it firsthand."

After 17 games within their own conference, the Sixers will finally see what their early success looks like against the other side.

#2642. LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over ‘Bron'

LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over 'Bron' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

It was another eventful week for LeBron James.

That's why we started the LeBron Log in the first place.

The King spent his latest week taking his teammates to the movies, fighting over his name in federal court and producing his best three-point shooting performance as a Sixer days after recording a podcast about the craft.

This week also marks 20 years since James faced the Sixers alongside Allen Iverson.

James found an appropriate choice for the Sixers' latest team outing.

He organized a private screening of I Play Rocky on Friday night for players, their families and members of the basketball operations staff. The film follows Sylvester Stallone's fight to get the original Rocky made while insisting that he play the title character.

"I mean, it's Rocky. We in Philly," James said. "I heard it was a great movie, and we had a night off. I've got a few connections, and I was able to bring that to my teammates and this organization for us to watch it. I thought it was a great movie. Unbelievably cast. Everyone looked like exactly who they were portraying. That is Hollywood for you. It was pretty cool."

The Sixers shared photos of James alongside Jaylen Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Labaron Philon Jr., Jabari Walker, Tacko Fall and Adem Bona.

"Movie night, courtesy of LeBron," the team wrote.

The nationwide release of I Play Rocky came less than two weeks before Philadelphia celebrates the 50th anniversary of the original film on Dec. 3.

Nick Nurse could not attend because of a previous commitment, but he received positive reviews from his players.

"They went, they said it was very good, they loved it," Nurse said. "The big takeaway was how much Anthony actually looked like Rocky. Or Sylvester Stallone. One in the same."

James' first season in Philadelphia now includes a private Rocky screening. A trip up the Art Museum steps remains available for a future edition.

James and Steve Nash devoted the latest episode of their Mind the Game podcast to the art of shooting.

The two examined shooting form, confidence, repetitions, free throws and some of their favorite jumpers. James also revealed one detail that can affect what he does after catching the ball.

"I'm a guy who don't like shooting against the laces," James said. "So sometimes I'll come up on a quick stop and I'm about to raise and I can feel the laces not fixed. I'll turn that into a pump fake."

The episode was released Nov. 17, while James was experiencing an extended struggle from three-point range. It did not provide an instant fix.

James went 1 for 5 from three against Orlando and missed his lone attempt against Milwaukee. He entered Monday night's meeting with Portland shooting 21.7 percent from deep through his first 13 games.

James made all three of his first-half attempts from three. He ended the second quarter by pump-faking, stepping to his left and beating the buzzer with a corner three that tied the game at 69.

Nobody could see where the laces sat on the catch. The pump fake was clear.

James finished 4 for 5 from three and scored a season-high 23 points on 8-for-13 shooting. It was his third consecutive game with at least 20 points, following 22 against Orlando and 21 against Milwaukee.

The Sixers lost to Portland, 128-111, but James produced his best long-range performance since joining them.

Six days after discussing the art of shooting, he provided a brief demonstration.

James is also attempting to protect one of his most recognizable nicknames.

James and LBJ Trademarks LLC filed a federal lawsuit on Nov. 17 against PlayVision Inc. and its founders over a sports-betting research app initially called "Bron."

The complaint alleges that the company used an AI-generated version of James in an advertisement without his permission. The figure wore a No. 23 jersey with "Bron" across the back and resembled James through its voice, build and tattoos.

It also scrolled through wagers involving NBA players.

The lawsuit alleges that the advertisement falsely created the impression that James endorsed the app and suggested that he considered betting on NBA games. The complaint said the video received roughly 1 million views before it was removed.

"The integrity of NBA competition, and the public's confidence that players are not betting on the games they play, is of paramount importance to the league, its players and its fans," the complaint said. "Any suggestion that an active NBA player is betting on NBA games is therefore far from a trivial matter, and it should not be used for clicks and views."

The app offered odds comparisons, betting trends and tracking tools but did not directly accept wagers, according to its developer.

PlayVision renamed it "Evie" on Nov. 18, one day after James filed the lawsuit. James is seeking an injunction and unspecified damages. The case remains active in the Southern District of New York.

CLEVELAND – NOVEMBER 25: LeBron James #23 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks to pass off when double teamed by the Philadelphia 76ers November 25, 2006 at The Quicken Loans Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. Copyright 2006 NBAE (Photo by David Liam Kyle/NBAE via Getty Images)

James spent Thanksgiving weekend in 2006 on the other side of the Sixers-Cavaliers matchup.

On Nov. 25, 2006, a 21-year-old James recorded 25 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one block in Cleveland's 108-95 win over Philadelphia.

Donning the Cavs' old-school orange threads, he played nearly 41 minutes.

Iverson led the Sixers with 31 points. Andre Iguodala added 17 points and eight rebounds, while Kyle Korver made three three-pointers off the bench.

James recorded 11 assists that night. Nearly 20 years later, another 11-assist performance against Indiana moved him past Jason Kidd for third place in NBA history.

The 2006 meeting also came near the end of Iverson's original run with Philadelphia. The Sixers traded him to Denver less than a month later.

James was 21. Iverson was nearing his departure.

Twenty years later, James is wearing a Sixers uniform and Iverson's No. 3 hangs above his home floor.

#2639. Bengals-Commanders clock error brings back memories of Steelers-Chargers clock error in 2015

Monday night’s game between the Bengals and Commanders ended with an apparent error by the clock operator. The same thing happened eleven years earlier, on a Monday night in October.

The Chargers were hosting the Steelers. Here’s the NFL’s official explanation, issued after the game:

“With 2:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, San Diego kicked off to Pittsburgh. The kick resulted in a touchback. By rule, the game clock does not start if the receiving team possesses the ball in the end zone and does not carry it into the field of play.

“Because of an error by the clock operator, the game clock was incorrectly started before the Steelers’ first play from scrimmage following the touchback. That first down snap came with 2:38 left to play instead of 2:56, a difference of 18 seconds.

“The official game time is kept on the stadium scoreboard, but it is the responsibility of the side judge to supervise the timing of the game. Had the side judge or any of the other six on-field officials noticed the timing error, they could have corrected it.

“The game clock is not subject to instant replay review unless there is a timing issue on the last play of the first half or the last play of the game. The performance of the clock operator and game officials will be reviewed per the standard procedure for reviewing every play of every game.”

The Steelers-Chargers situation shows that, when a clock error happens, the side judge becomes responsible for not catching it. On Monday night, that role was filled by Jimmy Buchanan. It was his job to ensure that the clock stopped when it was supposed to stop.

What comes next remains to be seen. In 2015, more than two years before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized gambling, the NFL interviewed the clock operator and side judge Rob Vernatchi.

The error in the 2015 game didn’t impact the outcome; the Steelers won the game, 24-20. Vernatchi was nevertheless suspended for a week. The NFL thereafter implemented the “right controls” to keep it from happening again.

It apparently happened again on Monday night, based on the information ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk shared after the game. Time, pun intended, will tell whether the league acknowledges the error and imposes discipline and/or conducts a broader investigation.

NFL insider reveals if teams called Browns about a Shedeur Sanders trade originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Cleveland Browns are locked into Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback going forward for the rest of the season, and for good reason. He's been playing great this year and is more than deserving of keeping the starting job.

But that has meant Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and, to a lesser degree, Taylen Green won't be seeing the field unless Watson is out. That, naturally, led to questions about whether Sanders would be drawing trade interest at the deadline or not.

Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported two weeks after the NFL trade deadline that the Browns did not field any calls about Sanders or Gabriel at the trade deadline, showing that teams didn't have much interest in either this season.

"The Browns received no trade calls on backup quarterbacks Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at or before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, league sources told Cleveland.com," Cabot reported.

Cleveland didn't field any trade offers for Sanders or Gabriel this year, even though both would seem to have been readily available had a team made a competitive offer.

#2636. James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers

James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James likes to refer to the NBA season as a "marathon."

A few miles in, the Sixers lead the Eastern Conference pack.

With 17 regular-season contests down of 82, the team sits at 14-3, which is 2.5 games ahead of the second-seeded Celtics. The Sixers squeaked out their latest win, a 132-129 decision Saturday over the cellar-dwelling Bucks, but the bottom line is they've become accustomed to finding many routes to victory.

"We want to build habits," James said. "We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity. I know sometimes it doesn't happen that way, but we want to do it.

"We want to strive to be as great as we can offensively, defensively and on special teams. A win is a win, but there's ways to win and ways to try to continue to build habits over the course of a marathon."

All sorts of Sixers games have gone down to the wire and they've won every single one.

The team is an incredible 12-0 in clutch situations, defined as games with a point differential of five or under in the final five minutes. The Sixers rank third in the NBA in clutch offensive rating (140.3) and third in clutch net rating (plus-42.0).

"It's good to build that part of our game," James said. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're going to be scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for 48 minutes. … We can learn from that."

James was the centerpiece of the Sixers' fourth-quarter offense Saturday. He scored 13 of his 21 points between the 7:46 and 3:13 mark of the fourth.

The four-time MVP got two buckets on no-nonsense drives and another on an after-timeout isolation hoop over rookie Brayden Burries. James also scored three times on a designed Horns action where he brought the ball up, used Tyrese Maxey's back screen at the elbow and caused serious problems for Milwaukee in the paint.

"We continue to add things to the half-court offense and also to the late-game package," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "That's something we added a few game ago. It's one of those things where, especially if we're in the bonus, we've got some big bodies that can cut down the lane and have feel for timing. It was working. Just keep going to it."

James has grown in comfort with Nurse's coaching style. He knows the Sixers expect him to be a de facto coach on the floor, too.

"I'm just trying to be there for the team in any capacity they want," he said. "Just trying to be an extension of his calls and his commands out there on the floor. Trying to make his life and his job a little bit easier as well.

"But it's been great, not only with him but the whole coaching staff. They've welcomed me with open arms and allowed me to kind of be the voice for the team every day, and take that responsibility."

After a tremendous first impression defensively and some subpar offensive nights, the Sixers' numbers have recently evened out.

The team is 12th in offensive rating outside of garbage time and 12th in defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. In essence, the Sixers have been a bit above average on both ends of the floor and downright brilliant in the closing minutes.

It's all added up to an early lead in a very long race.

"I think we've bought into the pass," James said. "We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels. … In order for us to be a super-complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious. And it's also key for our other guys, to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident. We've done that from Day 1 and I think it's gotten better and better. … And I think our defense has been really good for the majority of the season.

"(Today) it wasn't so great, but we've been very good defensively throughout the course of the season. … I don't want to say there's anything bad. There's so many things for us to do better for sure. There's games where we can defensive rebound a lot better and there's games where we can not turn the ball over (as much). And there's games where we can be a little more phsyical defensively at the point of attack like (today).

"I wouldn't say anything has been bad, though. That's a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement and we don't want to be great in November. That would be weird."

#2630. Todd Bowles says Buccaneers must fix late-game errors

Todd Bowles knows the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are close.

The Buccaneers' record is just 3-7 following their latest loss to the Detroit Lions, falling by a score of 31-21. However, the score doesn't tell the whole story, as Tampa Bay trailed 17-14 entering the fourth quarter. Furthermore, it was the first time the Buccaneers had lost by more than one possession all season. In all six prior losses, they had been by one possession.

After a dominant two-game win streak that saw them outscore their NFC South opponents 59-13, Tampa Bay is now on a two-game losing streak to NFC North opponents, the Lions and Chicago Bears. In defense of the Buccaneers, they're arguably two of the top teams in the conference.

During his Monday press conference availability, reporters asked Bowles what it will take for the Buccaneers to start playing better in the fourth quarter. Unsurprisingly, Bowles -- who is in his fifth season as head coach -- kept it simple.

"Got to be able to finish, minimize the mistakes on both sides of the ball, all three phases, really," said Bowles. "You got to minimize the mistakes. You got to win field position, and you got to execute."

The Buccaneers are in second place in the NFC South with the Panthers at 5-5. The catch is that the Buccaneers currently hold the tiebreaker and can keep it at the end of the season by beating Carolina at home on Monday Night Football next week.

"Yeah, they're aware of it -- they understand it," Bowles said of the Buccaneers needing to have urgency this week. "They know where we stand, and you know it starts with us in this room. So we got to correct everything and turn that thing around, and we got to do it a game at a time."

With the Buccaneers having six one-possession losses this season, they'll have to learn to close out games in this final stretch. That will have to start in Week 12 when they face the division-leading Panthers.

#2626. Healthy Rams pass rushing unit targeting 'Fearsome' performance vs. Packers

Myles Garrett appreciates football history and, apparently, etymology.

Long before the star edge rusher joined the Rams in June, he studied Deacon Jones, the Rams' Hall of Fame end who was a member of the team's "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line of the 1960s and first dubbed the act of violently tackling a quarterback behind the line of scrimmage a sack.

Garrett, a 10th-year pro, said that when he was in high school he watched programs and interviews that featured Jones.

"Listening to him speak, him coining the term 'sack', how much he's done for this game and how special he was at the time in which he played," said Garrett, who also incorporated Jones' famed head-slap move into his prep pass-rushing repertoire.

On Wednesday, the Rams will honor that era when they don for the first time "Fearsome White" uniforms for their game against the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium.

The new white and blue ensemble pays homage to the Rams' front that featured ends Jones and Lamar Lundy and tackles Merlin Olsen and Rosey Grier.

Grier, 94, will be in attendance along with family members of some of the deceased players that made up the legendary line.

"They set the tone," said Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald, an eight-time All-Pro. "Obviously, you know how that group played together, the standard they set.

"Coming here as a rookie you heard about it. I always try to live up to their success and everything they were able to do."

Wednesday's game marks the first time this season that the Rams will deploy a front that includes Garrett and edge rusher Byron Young, and linemen Donald, Braden Fiske and Kobie Turner.

Turner is back after sitting out four games because of a groin injury.

"Perfect timing," he said, "Fearsome Foursome week."

Sacks did not become an official NFL statistic until 1982. According to ProFootballReference.com, Jones' 173½ unofficial sacks ranks third all-time behind Bruce Smith (200) and Reggie White (198).

Garrett (128½) is 27th, Donald (112½) 42nd.

The Rams have 21 sacks, which ranks 20th among 32 NFL teams. Young has a team-best 5½ sacks. Garrett, who amassed an NFL season-record 23 sacks for the Cleveland Browns last season, has three in three games. Fiske has 2½, Donald 1½ and Turner is searching for his first.

But to this point, those players were not available at the same time.

Donald, a three-time NFL defensive player of the year, did not play in the season-opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia because he was still acclimating after coming out of retirement. Garrett, a two-time NFL defensive player of the year, sat out the next seven games recovering from knee surgery. Then Turner was injured.

Now they are together, along with edge rushers Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey and linemen Tyler Davis, Ty Hamilton and Larrell Murchison.

On a night when the rock band U2 will provide halftime entertainment, members of the Rams' defensive front aim to put on their own show to honor the Fearsome Foursome's legacy.

"They set the standard for what that means," Fiske said, "but for us to be that next generation of pass rushers, it's cool to be part of group that's special."

Rams pass rushers Myles Garrett (95) and Aaron Donald (99) celebrate between Braden Fiske, left, and Byron Young during a win over the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8. (Scott Taetsch / Getty Images)

Young said he was honored to wear a uniform that salutes the past.

"I know we're not there yet — how good they were — but just being in the conversation is pretty cool," he said.

Coach Sean McVay said the Fearsome Foursome set a standard for how the defensive front can impose its will. And the uniforms the Rams will wear to honor them "look pretty swaggy too," he said.

Garrett is looking forward to the opportunity.

"It means a lot to be able to wear that uniform and wear those colors," Garrett said, "and hopefully make them proud."

#2624. Lakers hit their top-10 defensive goal — at least for one night

The Lakers have made one of their biggest goals very clear.

They want to be a top-10 rated defensive team.

Well, they skyrocketed from being rated 15th defensively Monday morning to 10th in the evening after a great defensive performance in their 109-94 win over the Jazz.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Collin Sexton, left, and forward Jake LaRavia defend Utah Jazz forward Brice Sensabaugh during an NBA game Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong

Sure, the Lakers have only played 18 games this season so a singular contest can wildly skew their defensive rating. And, they've found themselves in this position after a win over the Jazz, who have the second-worst record in the Western Conference at 3-16.

But, hey, at least for one night, they've reached their target.

"How many points did they score?" Walker Kessler inquired when he was asked about the team's defensive performance Monday.

After being told just 94, the Lakers' defensive anchor talked about how the team has made major strides on the less glamorous side of the court.

Ace Bailey (19) of the Utah Jazz shoots against Walker Kessler (14) and Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. Getty Images

"Yeah, you know, I would say that's pretty good defense," said Kessler, who had 10 points, 12 rebounds and two blocked shots against the Jazz. "I think our transition defense has gotten better, which is nice to see. Our limiting second chance points has gotten better. Obviously, we can still improve on that. We're kind of struggling right now with open 3s."

This is a positive development for the Lakers, who were obviously going to be a great offensive team behind Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, but had a lot of questions on the defensive end.

But over the last five games without Reaves, who has been sidelined because of a left heel bruise, they've been forced to tighten things up on the defensive end while having a 25-point hole on offense.

Kyle Filipowski of the Utah Jazz drives against Jake LaRavia and Matisse Thybulle of the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images

Funny enough, the Lakers have said since training camp that their defense is underrated. They've said their wings have been underestimated. They said that they could be good.

Well, they're showing signs that they weren't exaggerating.

We all knew that Kessler was an elite rebounder and rim defender. But now we're seeing that the Lakers are deeper than we may have thought on defense. From top to bottom, everyone is grinding and scrapping, including Doncic, who has received a lot of criticism throughout his career for only focusing on offense.

It's good news for the Lakers, who are tied for the best record in the NBA at 15-3. They have the No. 3-rated offense in the NBA. And at least for one night, they can say that they're in the top-10 on both sides of the court.

"I'm happy," Kessler said. "I think we're trending upwards, and that's all you want to see."
