#2615. Tennessee Fined $250K After Fans Pelted LSU Coach Lane Kiffin with Golf Balls and Mustard

Tennessee was fined $250K for their fans' conduct during the school's game against LSU

Lane Kiffin and LSU were pelted with golf balls and bottles of mustard during their game against Tennessee

Tennessee fans didn't hold the mustard — or roll out the welcome mat — for Lane Kiffin in his return to Neyland Stadium.

The LSU coach was the target of golf balls, boos and bottles of the yellow condiment, all of which resulted in the school receiving a $250,000 fine handed down from the Southeastern Conference (SEC).

The conference said in a statement on Sunday, Nov. 22 that Tennessee was assessed the fine for "interruption of its November 21 football game with Louisiana State University due to fans throwing debris onto the field." The SEC added that fans' behavior ended up "interrupting the competitive opportunity for both teams and endangering contest participants."

Kiffin, 51, coached the Volunteers in 2009 before he left for USC, and he seemingly has few fans left in Knoxville some 17 years later.

Fans dressed up as bottles of mustard at the Tennessee-LSU game.Credit: Cal Sport Media via AP Images

With 3:14 left in the game — and as the Vols cruised to a 27-13 victory — fans in the Tennessee student section threw golf balls at the Tigers' bench.

The game was stopped for several minutes and LSU moved to the center of the field to avoid getting pelted by the detritus.

Saturday's decision to throw mustard and golf balls harkens back to what students threw at Kiffin in 2021 when he returned then, as the coach at Ole Miss.

Kiffin, who is in his first year as LSU's head coach and is sporting a 6-5 record, sparked similar sentiment when he abandoned the Rebels for Baton Rouge last year.

#2614. The Lakers are ‘optimistic’ Austin Reaves will return from injury against Spurs

After suffering a bruised heel on Nov. 11 against the Milwaukee Bucks, Austin Reaves has missed the Los Angeles Lakers' past five games. But according to head coach JJ Redick, it sounds like Reaves is progressing well and nearing a return as soon as the Lakers' next game against the San Antonio Spurs on Friday.

"We want to be consistent with our [return to play] stuff," Redick told reporters prior to Monday's win over the Utah Jazz. "I think today was a big step just in terms of getting a stay ready game in and he played great, moved great. We're optimistic for the rest of this week."

Although the Lakers have won four of five without Reaves in the lineup, they'll certainly welcome him back as quickly as possible. Three of those four wins occurred against the Jazz, Sacramento Kings and Charlotte Hornets, which own a combined 9-43 record this season. Their one loss during that stretch came to Utah on the second leg of a back-to-back as well. Even with those four wins against lottery-bound opponents, their play has suffered since Reaves became sidelined.

Through the first 13 games of the year — Reaves played in 12 of them — they were 11-2 with a plus-9.0 net rating (fifth league-wide) and the top-ranked offense (122.5 points per 100 possession). Over the past five contests, they're 4-1 with a plus-4.3 net rating (10th) and the 17th-ranked offense (114.0 points per 100).

Much of that offensive downswing stems from Luka Dončić's five-game slump (53.2% true shooting, 5.2 turnovers per game since Reaves went down). But it's entirely plausible Reaves' absence is creating too hefty of a workload for Dončić to endure. His return should better balance and diversify Los Angeles' offense by easing some of Dončić's burden for the betterment of everyone.

The timing is ideal, too. The Lakers' schedule significantly ramps up over the next five weeks. Across a 13-game stretch spanning from Friday through Dec. 29, the Lakers face the Spurs, Rockets (x2), Timberwolves (x2), Denver Nuggets (x2), Memphis Grizzlies (x2), Philadelphia 76ers and Indiana Pacers, which could have Tyrese Haliburton back by that Dec. 21 matchup.

#2608. Resurfaced clip reveals Michael Jordan link that changed Kobe Bryant’s entire career

Kobe Bryant's career trajectory changed because of Michael Jordan.

Lower Merion's Kobe Bryant goes to the net at the Palestra in a Feb 27, 1996 playoff game against Coatsville. MediaNews Group via Getty Images

In a clip from a 2024 appearance on Byron Scott's "Fast Break" podcast, former NBA player John Salley recalled Bryant explaining why he skipped college and entered the 1996 NBA Draft directly out of high school.

Bryant was selected 13th overall in the 1996 NBA Draft by the Charlotte Hornets and was immediately traded to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Kobe Bryant(L) and Chicago Bulls guard Michael Jordan(R) talk during a free-throw attempt during the fourth quarter 17 December at the United Center in Chicago. AFP/Getty Images

Lakers #24 Kobe Bryant pumps his fist during the fourth quarter. Anthony J. Causi

Jordan ultimately continued playing for Chicago through 1998. After retiring for a second time, he returned with the Washington Wizards in 2001 and permanently ended his career in 2003.

#2604. Three former Falcons advance in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting

The voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027 is underway, as the Hall continues to narrow down its list of candidates ahead of February's NFL Honors.

On Tuesday, the Hall announced that 52 players have advanced to the next round of voting, with three former Atlanta Falcons among them, all of whom are deserving of a spot in Canton: Tommy Nobis, John Abraham and Billy "White Shoes" Johnson.

It's long overdue for "Mr. Falcon" to receive his gold jacket. The first-ever draft selection in franchise history, Nobis spent his entire 11-year NFL career with the Falcons from 1966-1976.

Nobis was named NFL Rookie of the Year in 1966, earned five trips to the Pro Bowl and was named to the NFL's 1960s All-Decade Team, despite entering the league midway through the decade. He led the Falcons in tackles in nine of his 11 seasons and was an inaugural member of the Falcons Ring of Honor in 2004. His No. 60 jersey is also retired by the franchise.

One of the best pass rushers in franchise history, Abraham spent seven seasons with the Falcons from 2006-2012, recording 68.5 sacks during his time in Atlanta, which remains an official franchise record.

Abraham finished his 15-year NFL career with 133.5 sacks, five Pro Bowl selections and two first-team All-Pro selections. "The Predator" recently received some well-deserved recognition from the franchise, as he was inducted into the Falcons Ring of Honor in October.

One of the most electrifying return specialists in NFL history, Johnson spent six seasons with the Falcons from 1982-1987. In 1983, Johnson earned his third career Pro Bowl selection and was named NFL Comeback Player of the Year. He also led the Falcons in receptions in both 1983 and 1985.

Perhaps most baffling is the fact that Johnson remains the only player named to the NFL's 75th Anniversary All-Time Team who has yet to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He was also named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team, as well as the 1970s and 1980s All-Decade Teams.

The list of 52 nominees will be narrowed down to 25 following the next round of voting, with the results expected to be announced in approximately two weeks. Hopefully, all three former Falcons will find themselves one step closer to football immortality in Canton, Ohio.

#2600. Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Antonio Brown among players advancing in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process for 2027 class

A pair of quarterbacks from the fabled 2004 draft class, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger and New York Giants icon Eli Manning, plus embattled wide receiver Antonio Brown, are among the 52 players the Pro Football Hall of Fame revealed are advancing in the voting process for the 2027 class.

Per current Hall of Fame bylaws, at this stage of that process, selectors cast ballots for 50 players they believe should move forward in their candidacy, but those tied for the 50th position also remain eligible for induction.

The list the Hall announced on Tuesday will next be cut down to 25 players. That more exclusive group will be unveiled in about two weeks.

For now, here's a position-by-position breakdown of the players being considered for enshrinement:

Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Ken Anderson

Shaun Alexander, Frank Gore, Marshawn Lynch, LeSean McCoy, Adrian Peterson, Fred Taylor, Ricky Watters

Anquan Boldin, Antonio Brown, Rob Gronkowski, Torry Holt, Billy "White Shoes" Johnson, Steve Smith Sr., Otis Taylor, Hines Ward, Reggie Wayne, Jason Witten

Rodney Harrison, Lester Hayes, Albert Lewis, Eddie Meador, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, Everson Walls, Darren Woodson

John Abraham, Geno Atkins, L.C. Greenwood, Jim Marshall, Robert Mathis, Haloti Ngata, Vince Wilfork, Kevin Williams

Maxie Baughan, London Fletcher, James Harrison, Karl Mecklenburg, Tommy Nobis, Terrell Suggs

Roethlisberger and Manning draw the eye, considering they each quarterbacked historic franchises to a pair of Super Bowl victories; however, this cohort is understandably littered with household names.

Running back Adrian Peterson is forever part of Minnesota Vikings lore. He's one of the nine NFL players to ever rush for 2,000 yards in a season. In fact, Peterson's 2,097 yards on the ground in 2012 were the second most in single-season league history, behind only the 2,105 rushing yards Eric Dickerson logged while starring for the Los Angeles Rams in 1984. Peterson earned NFL MVP honors that season.

Another RB in the running, Frank Gore, is the NFL's third all-time leading rusher. Gore spent the bulk of his career with the San Francisco 49ers. Even in his 16th and final campaign, he was still somewhat productive, amassing 653 rushing yards in his age-37 season with the New York Jets back in 2020.

Rob Gronkowski and Jason Witten are both integral to the annals of tight end play. Gronkowski was a red-zone monster, finishing his 11-season career with a whopping 92 receiving touchdowns. Together, he and seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback Tom Brady authored one of the most electrifying duos in the sport, first with the New England Patriots and then with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As for Witten, he proved to be one of the NFL's most reliable security blankets to date, maxing out with 110 catches during his 2012 campaign with the Dallas Cowboys.

Interestingly, beleaguered wideout Antonio Brown was among the players included in 52-man list the Hall put forth on Tuesday. Brown was a superstar during the peak of his head-scratching 12-season run in the league. He built most of his résumé in Pittsburgh, where he stacked seven 1,000-yard receiving seasons. In his nine-season stay with the Steelers, he led the NFL in receiving yards twice: first in 2014 and again in 2017. He also led the league in touchdown catches in 2018.

But the end of Brown's career was marred by the trouble he got himself into, on and off the field. Earlier this month, in a Miami court, Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault following a 2025 shooting incident.

Brown still has long odds of being inducted next year. Ultimately, 13 players will make up most of the 15 finalists who will be presented at the selection committee's annual meeting. The other two candidates will be Bill Belichick (who emerged from the "coach" category) and Patriots owner Robert Kraft (who came out of the "contributor" category).

The Hall's 2027 class will be announced at "NFL Honors" in February.

Speaking to reporters before practice on Tuesday, Vrabel succinctly stated that the defense needs to clean things up moving forward, per Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller.

"Just got to do everything a bit better," Vrabel admitted.

The Patriots struggled defensively from Weeks 9-10, raising questions about its potency against high-powered offenses in the league. New England surrendered 45 points to Green Bay in its Week 9 loss to the Packers, struggling particularly in pass coverage. Packers star wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combined for 335 receiving yards, with cornerback Christian Gonzalez having been responsible for much of their significant production.

New England's defensive struggles continued in Week 10 against Detroit, as the unit allowed the Lions to score 35 points. The defensive line and linebacker units were not able to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs, who finished with 252 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. Amon-Ra St. Brown also gave the secondary problems, recording four receptions for 98 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots' loss to the Lions.

With the team's next matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers approaching on Sunday, the Patriots' defense faces an important opportunity to turn the tide. Vrabel will need to see considerable improvement from the unit if New England hopes to avoid another hit to their dwindling playoff hopes.

#2594. NBA News: Donte DiVincenzo Cleared for Practice

The Minnesota Timberwolves officially announced on Tuesday morning that Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for team basketball activities. As further detailed by The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski, a source told him that DiVincenzo is eyeing a return in January 2027.

ESPN's Shams Charania also shared his update on DiVincenzo's potential timeline, going on record as saying closed to around the turn of the new year.

This may not be a surprise to those of you who have been following along his rehab journey. As mentioned earlier this month, the Wolves have been providing a mini-docuseries on their YouTube channel following him along as he progresses towards a return titled "Day Zero." It's an incredible series that I highly recommend you check out if you haven't already done so.

During those updates, fans could only read between the lines and choose to believe the edited content that the media team was putting out about DiVincenzo's recovery. However, today's headline is an official update. Though the team's official press release didn't mention a specific timetable, it seems awfully realistic to expect him back within two months from now. It would be the quickest recovery from a torn Achilles tendon in NBA history.

In Krawczynski's article, he shared a quote from Donte's teammate Jaylen Clark, who also suffered a torn Achilles in college.

"He's light years ahead of me," Clark said in October. "Like, it's crazy to watch him on a daily basis. It's just crazy how far technology and all that stuff (has come), because I don't know, he's at six, seven months. The stuff he's doing, I was nowhere near. It took me a year and three months, four months. And then at that point, I was still out of shape, fat, barely could jump and everything. He's flying around."

Until we actually see Donte's name off the daily injury report, we can't quite say he's making history yet. But it's becoming clear that his hard work is setting things up for him to completely reshape what it means when a NBA player suffers what many used to consider a career-ending injury. January looks realistic, but what if it's even December? Sleigh bells? Presents under the tree? I hear what the comments section is whispering.

This update is certainly something Wolves fans should be happy to hear, considering the meltdown that many had regarding Anthony Edwards' media availability last week. Couple that with the hamstring issue Jaylen Clark recently suffered, getting some reinforcements back would be amazing. The second half of December features a slew of games against Western Conference playoff teams like the Lakers, Nuggets, and Thunder. Minnesota has been able to stay afloat despite missing several rotation players, but will that be sustainable moving forward?

Donte plays a style that is incredibly easy to fit in no matter who's on the floor or what the system is. He's a high energy "do-shit" player that will hustle on both ends of the court. His propensity to dive around the court fits Minnesota's style of defense like a glove. Meanwhile, on the offensive end, adding another movement shooter will make an already deadly bench deadlier. It's no wonder why many in the organization, front office and players, view him as the "heart and soul" of the team.

I'm going to take a second to gloat about my prediction resumé from earlier this month. Before there was an official update on DiVincenzo's return to practice status, I bravely put my name on the line.

I'll wager 690 Hoopus Points that Donte is back on the court before the All-Star break. I'll even call my shot and say he makes his debut on January 27th, 2027 against the team he suffered his injury against, the Denver Nuggets.

Well, well, well. Who do you believe? The comments section (Christmas), Charania (New Year), Krawczynski (January), or Sun (January 27, 2027)?

#2593. Torino-Lazio, Rodriguez torna dopo la sanzione: difesa in emergenza

Il difensore svizzero aveva risposto alla convocazione della Nazionale nonostante la lesione tendinea.

Ricardo Rodriguez è stato sanzionato dal Torino ed escluso dalla trasferta a Napoli per una scelta della società, non per problemi fisici. Secondo quanto riferisce La Stampa, il difensore svizzero tornerà utile sabato contro la Lazio, dopo aver scontato la sanzione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La squadra di Ignazio Abate affronta la capolista guidata da Gennaro Gattuso dopo essere scivolata al tredicesimo posto. I granata hanno raccolto appena un punto nelle ultime quattro giornate, dopo una serie di tre vittorie consecutive a ottobre. Per il tecnico, al debutto in Serie A, la partita rappresenta un’occasione per invertire la rotta.

La Stampa presenta così il momento del tecnico e la sfida di sabato: «Toro, tutti i dolori del giovane Abate: serve coraggio per uscire dalla crisi. Il tecnico chiamato a rialzare la squadra: sabato con la capolista Lazio si gioca la grande chance».

Il quotidiano richiama le difficoltà nella costruzione del gioco: 15 gol segnati in 12 giornate. Nell’analisi delle scelte tattiche di Abate scrive: «Tra errori banali, baricentro basso e poca lucidità negli ultimi 25 metri, Abate paga lo scotto del noviziato e l'abbandono del 3-4-2-1 estivo per il più prudente 3-5-2. Servirà il contributo dei senatori come Simeone, Adams e Vlasic e la stessa determinazione mostrata da Lucas Perri, capace di riscattarsi dopo un avvio difficile fino a fare la differenza al Maradona».

La Lazio è allenata da Gattuso, che in passato era stato cercato dallo stesso Cairo.

L’esclusione di Rodriguez dalla trasferta partenopea è legata a una vicenda disciplinare. Il difensore, reduce da una lesione tendinea, non avrebbe mantenuto la promessa di curarsi al Filadelfia durante la sosta, scegliendo invece di rispondere alla convocazione della Svizzera.

La Stampa ricostruisce così la decisione del club: «Il Toro punisce Rodriguez: una lezione per lo spogliatoio. Il difensore svizzero non è rimasto a Torino per problemi fisici, bensì per scelta della società dopo non aver mantenuto la promessa di curarsi al Filadelfia durante la sosta. Pur reduce da una lesione tendinea, Rodriguez ha preferito rispondere alla chiamata della Svizzera per tagliare il traguardo delle 150 presenze contro la Scozia, scatenando il confronto con il ds Petrachi e lo stop punitivo».

#2589. Player-turned-doctor Laurent Duvernay-Tardif is working with the Chiefs' medical staff

Former Chiefs offensive lineman Laurent Duvernay-Tardif, who got his medical degree while playing in the NFL, is back in Kansas City working with the Chiefs’ medical staff.

“Feeling privileged to be back on the sidelines, this time shadowing the medical team to gain experience in sports medicine and on-field emergency response,” Duvernay-Tardif wrote on social media.

A native of Quebec who has been completing medical training there since retiring from the NFL, Duvernay-Tardif is currently spending a month with the Chiefs’ medical staff to learn more about treatment of athletes.

#2588. Donovan Mitchell on 9-9 Cavs' inconsistent effort: 'I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN'

The Chicago Bulls entered Thanksgiving week as one of the NBA's worst teams: 4-12, getting outscored by nearly eight points per 100 possessions, with the second-worst defense in the NBA. And yet, they controlled the bulk of Monday's matchup with the Cleveland Cavaliers, leading for nearly the entire final three quarters — and by as many as 24 points — in a 122-108 win.

This, despite the Cavs coming in with a rest advantage, with the Bulls on the second night of a back-to-back after going to overtime against the Nuggets on Sunday. And despite Chicago being without leading scorer Norman Powell, who's stuck in street clothes nursing a strained right hamstring, and 2026 lottery pick Caleb Wilson, out with a broken right hand. And despite a pair of Chicago starters — point guard Josh Giddey and swingman Matas Buzelis — getting benched, again, late in the fourth quarter by first-year head coach Tiago Splitter, who elected to close with backup point guard Tre Jones and intriguing two-way reserve Jaylin Sellers. (Giddey did not seem particularly pleased about that.)

And, perhaps most importantly, despite the Cavs … well, frankly, they're just supposed to be better than this.

Donovan Mitchell (right), James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers have stumbled to .500 a month into the season.

Yes, Cleveland's without Evan Mobley, an integral component of its operations on both sides of the floor. And yes, Kenny Atkinson's club wound up on the business end of Chicago going 20-for-49 from 3-point range while the Cavs made just eight of their 31 triple tries. Not exactly easy to win when you're outscored by 36 points from long distance.

It's not just the simple, cruel vicissitudes of shooting variance, though. Aside from Mobley, the Cavs had the entire rest of their preferred rotation against a four-win team … and they still got drilled. A Cleveland squad that made it to the Eastern Conference finals last spring enters Wednesday's matchup with the New York Knicks — the team that, as you might recall, annihilated the Cavs in that series en route to winning the NBA championship — at 9-9, in seventh place in the East.

That's a long way from where the Cavs — one of the most expensive rosters in the sport — want to be … and, from the sound of things, they've got some pretty big questions to answer before they can get there. From Danny Cunningham of The Inside Shot:

Donovan Mitchell, who had a game-high 28 points, was asked about the effort being inconsistent from quarter-to-quarter or game-to-game this season.

Mitchell thought for a full five seconds after the question was asked.

"I think," he said before pausing for eight more seconds. "I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN."

"I think the biggest thing now is just figuring each other out. We're not here in the locker room panicking, and all I can say to that, is what we got going forward. Nights like tonight are bad. It's a bad night, and we got to respond to that. We've got to respond to that and just keep playing our game. There's so many different things you can point to, but at the end of the day for us, it's within us. I have all the confidence in everybody in here, and we've got all the confidence in each other. We've got to go out there and execute it. That doesn't really answer your question, but yeah."

If there's one thing I'm qualified to assess as a longtime professional blogger, it's this: That was a lot of words to not really make any point or address the issue at hand. Which, come to think of it, might constitute a pretty loud statement about the state of affairs in Cleveland right about now.

Mitchell wasn't the only Cavalier searching for an answer to the issues that have characterized the club's fits-and-starts opening to the season. Peyton Watson, the swingman who came over from Denver in an offseason sign-and-trade intended to plug Cleveland's long-yawning hole on the wing, offered a somewhat more direct answer than the All-NBA scoring guard.

"I think if we knew the answer, we would just do it," Watson said in the locker room. "I think we're still searching for that. You know, I'm always trying to communicate with my teammates and try to help make their job easier and just be a guy that connects the team in a lot of ways. I think I try to just go out there and lead by example by playing as hard as I can every night. I just think that everybody has got to look inward and look themselves in the mirror and ask themselves, 'Am I giving it 100% every single night?' I think that if that's not the case, then we need to go to the drawing board and really, like I said, look in the mirror and evaluate ourselves."

That doesn't exactly seem like the most stirring vote of confidence for the competitive makeup of the Cavaliers, especially considering they've already gone through a few moments that would seem to invite such sober self-reflection.

Blowing a 29-point lead against the 76ers on opening night. Dropping both ends of a home-and-home to the post-injury-apocalypse Thunder. Getting boat-raced by the Knicks in the second half at home, an extension of the pain of the conference finals. Getting blown out by a Hornets team playing without Brandon Miller or Kon Knueppel. Getting out-executed down the stretch by a Grizzlies squad playing without Ty Jerome. And now, Monday's scattershot effort in Chicago.

It just feels like something's missing in Cleveland, some spark, some urgency — and it starts on the defensive end.

The last half-decade of success for the Cavs — a climb out of the post-LeBron basement that began with the Mobley/Allen/Darius Garland unit under J.B. Bickerstaff, and that continued after the trade for Mitchell made it a "core four" — had been predicated on consistently stout defenses, with Cleveland ranking in the top eight in points allowed per possession each season from 2021 through 2025. That began to shift when Atkinson's arrival supercharged the offense, and more firmly tilted after dealing for Harden; Cleveland posted a top-five offense after the trade deadline, but a below-average defense, and got routinely torched by the Knicks in the four-game conference finals sweep.

The Cavs now sit at 21st in defensive efficiency — on pace for their first bottom-10 finish on that end since 2020-21. They're conceding shots at the rim and from beyond the 3-point line more regularly, and they give up wide-open 3s at a bottom-10 rate. (Nearly half of Chicago's 3-point attempts on Monday came without a Cavalier defender within 6 feet of the shooter.) They don't force turnovers, and they're average-at-best at clearing the defensive glass and guarding without fouling. That's a recipe for underwhelming results, unless you can balance out that bottom-10 defense with a No. 1-with-a-bullet offense … which the Cavs, currently a good-but-not-overwhelming seventh in points scored per possession, don't have at the moment.

Maybe they will. Get Mobley healthy, get Harden — who followed up his 51-point Friday masterclass by shooting 5-for-14 from the floor with seven turnovers in Chicago — more consistently off the schneid, and get Watson (a career-low 48% on 2-pointers and 27% on 3s) thawed out, and maybe these Cavs have the ingredients they need to build on last season's trip to the final four and put themselves in position to make a bid to represent the East in the NBA Finals. They believe they have the talent to do that.

Right now, though, they feel like a team that's less than the sum of its parts — a group that's playing like it's just kind of going through the motions until the real season starts, rather than one that needs to earn its postseason spot in an East that's gotten more crowded at the top. And if the Cavs want to have a shot at being the last team standing come springtime, they need to start finding answers as fall turns to winter.

"You can't just turn it on in April or May," Cavs guard Sam Merrill told reporters. "I think building the right habits only makes it easier to play that way once you get to later in the season and in the playoffs. We continue to talk about it. That's got to continue to be our mindset."

Talking about it is one thing. Their next chance to do something about it comes Wednesday in New York. One bit of good news for Mitchell and Co., at least? The game won't air on ESPN.

#2585. Connecticut football traditions, rivalries return to Thanksgiving week for eight old and new matchups

When the Bullard-Havens and Bassick football teams kick off at 6 p.m. Tuesday, it will mark the return of an old tradition. The two teams have a long history, much of which took place on Thanksgiving, dating as far back as the 1960s.

It's a history the teams are embracing for Thanksgiving week once again even in the name. The game is being dubbed "The Frank Brown Bowl" in honor of the former Bridgeport educator and Bassick coach.

"We want Thanksgiving football to always mean something to the kids," said Bullard-Havens coach Derrick Lewis, who has also coached at Bassick. "Any time you're dealing with a city type of a deal, all the kids are friends with one another, they all know each other, and they all support each other too, which is pretty cool.

The two schools had played on Thanksgiving up until 2016 and that's also the last time Bassick had a game on the holiday week until this year.

"It's great for Bridgeport to play Bridgeport on Thanksgiving week," Bassick coach Desmond Lymon said. "It's been a while since we last played and it brings a sense of pride into the city."

The Bassick vs. Bullard-Havens matchup is one of eight games during the holiday week which were not on last year's slate. They're games that are either returning, brand new, or in some cases rivalries that are joining the Thanksgiving tradition.

Bassick vs. Bullard-Havens at Kennedy Stadium, 6 p.m.

Thames River co-op at Montville/St. Bernard, 6 p.m.

Like Bassick and Bullard-Havens, the Wilton at Ridgefield match-up is a natural fit.

Wilton had been playing Trinity Catholic for Thanksgiving, but after Trinity closed after the 2019 season, the Warriors were left without a partner. They settled on a revolving series of teams such as Shelton, Xavier and Hillhouse the week before the holiday.

EJ DiNunzio was hired as Wilton's head coach in 2018 and said he had wanted to get the Ridgefield game back because of the rivalry between the schools.

However, Ridgefield had an ongoing Thanksgiving matchup with Danbury and Tigers' head coach Jamie Reed said they didn't want to leave the Hatters out in the cold.

Then in 2025, Tim Smith, a Danbury assistant coach, became the head coach at ATI, a co-op of Danbury schools Abbott Tech and Immaculate.

This season, ATI is set to play Danbury, opening the door for the Wilton-Ridgefield matchup.

"When I told the kids, they were so excited," DiNunzio said. "I'd been talking about it for a couple of years, and it was like 'yeah coach, you didn't get it again this year, we're not getting it.' So when I was finally able to tell them we finally had it secured, they went nuts."

DiNunzio added that as a traditionalist, his preference would have been to play Thursday, but he's happy having the game back during the holiday week.

"It's a great football game whenever we play it and now, it's even better because we can get the alumni back and involved," DiNunzio said.

Reed said Ridgefield athletic director Dane Street deserves a lot of credit for making the game happen.

Reed also said he got a taste of what the holiday game means while watching a junior varsity contest between the Tigers and Warriors.

"Because the Ridgefield-Wilton game has been kind of inconsistent the last few years, I was worried it might not have as much juice this season," Reed said. "But I was at the JV game this past Saturday and both sides picked up right where we left off."

Dominoes falling into place have led to other new match-ups.

Windham is facing Woodstock Academy, with the Whippets' former Thanksgiving partner, Montville, now co-opping with St. Bernard, facing the Thames River co-op.

The Gilbert/Northwestern/Housatonic co-op had played St. Paul in the past, but with St. Paul now in a co-op with Avon, GNH is playing the Nonnewaug co-op. Both teams are in the Berkshire League for other sports.

CREC and SMSA will also square off after facing other teams in recent seasons.

South Windsor and Enfield have played each other in the final game of the regular season since 2016, after Enfield and Fermi combined into one school.

It's called the Route 5 Rivalry, and the trophy is currently in the hands of South Windsor, which won the game last fall.

When Enfield hosts the game, they play during the Thanksgiving week.

Enfield coach James Lyver said he feels it's important to honor the Thanksgiving tradition in Enfield, after the Eagles had faced Fermi on the holiday for 37 years.

"It's great to bring our town together to honor our graduating senior football players, cheerleaders and band members," Lyver said. "It is also extremely important to the residents to reconnect with old friends and classmates around the Thanksgiving holiday."

The alumni factor is also something Lewis pointed to regarding the Bassick vs. Bullard-Havens game.

"It's funny, I've been coaching for so long now, I've actually coached fathers and uncles and cousins," Lewis said. "It's easy to talk about the great players and the great teams of the past. Our school doesn't have as much of a winning history as the other schools, I think we've had four All-Staters in our program, Josh Headley being one of them. We've had a chance to talk about tradition and we don't take anything lightly.

"I know they've struggled this year and we've had our struggles too but it's all thrown out during Thanksgiving."

#2583. Alperen Sengun heading towards third straight NBA All-Star game

The new NBA season is still pretty young, but some things are slowly coming into focus, and one of them is the potential NBA All-Star participants. The Houston Rockets' Alperen Sengun is in the midst of perhaps his finest season to date, and people are really taking notice. In fact, ESPN just recently named their top potential All-Star participants, and Sengun was listed in the top four. Here's what they had to say about Alpie:

"Trivia time: Who is the leading scorer for the NBA's most efficient offense?

Somehow, the answer is Sengun, who is posting a career-best 22.1 points per game for a balanced Rockets attack that has all five starters averaging in double digits.

While Fred VanVleet's return from injury has shifted Kevin Durant into a slightly lower-usage role, the 24-year-old Sengun has remained a central part of Houston's offense. The Turkish big man ranks in the top five leaguewide by PER and win shares, and he has dished more assists than any center besides, well …"

That center is obviously Sengun's idol Nikola Jokic. But Sengun is having a very Jokic-like season, averaging 21.9 points now, 9.2 rebounds, 7 assists and 1 steal per game. Sengun is shooting 55.1 percent from the field and is shooting 50 percent on triples while putting up 2 attempts per game. It's not a full breakout due to Houston's egalitarian offense, but Kevin Durant's willingness to take a back seat has been good for Sengun and the Rockets.

#2578. Tiger Woods’ Sun Day Red dealt setback in trademark fight over leaping tiger logo

A divided federal appeals court on Tuesday ordered the dismissal of a trademark lawsuit by Tiger Woods' golf apparel company, which sought approval to use its "leaping tiger" logo after another company with a similar logo objected.

Reversing a lower court ruling, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals in Pasadena, California, said courts in that state lacked jurisdiction to consider claims by Woods' Sun Day Red against Tigeraire, a Louisiana company that makes cooling fans attachable to athletes' headgear.

The 2-1 majority said this was because Tigeraire, which is affiliated with the Louisiana State University Tigers, had no physical presence in California and did little business there.

More: What your golf fit says about you: Sun Day Red

Tuesday's decision does not affect Tigeraire's trademark infringement lawsuit against Sunday Red, which has been on hold.

Lawyers for both companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Sunday Red, based in San Clemente, California, is part of TaylorMade Golf, which is a subsidiary of South Korean private equity firm Centroid Investment Partners.

Sun Day Red, as Woods' brand is known, launched in February 2024, paying homage to Woods' wearing red on Sunday during golf tournaments.

Its logo contains 15 stripes, one for each of Woods' major championship titles.

Shortly after Sun Day Red's launch, Tigeraire, which launched in 2020, sent a cease-and-desist letter that said the competing logos were confusing consumers. Settlement talks failed, prompting the dueling lawsuits.

Sunday Red's lawsuit sought a declaration it did nothing wrong, and accused Tigeraire of seeking an "unwarranted financial windfall from a larger and more successful brand." A federal judge refused to dismiss the case, and Tigeraire appealed.

Writing for Tuesday's majority, Circuit Judge Morgan Christen called Tigeraire's sales in California "trivial," totaling just 80 products over eight months and including only one item of apparel, a T-shirt.

She also called the cease-and-desist letter a "garden-variety" attempt to begin settlement talks, which did not support asserting jurisdiction.

Circuit Judge Milan Smith dissented. He said the majority was too quick to dismiss Sunday Red's claim it could face irreparable harm if forced to pull products from stores and rebrand itself while Tigeraire asserted its trademark rights.

Woods, 50, launched Sun Day Red after his 27-year partnership with Nike NKE.N ended.

This article originally appeared on Golfweek: Tiger Woods' Sun Day Red dealt setback in trademark fight over leaping tiger logo

#2577. Steve Kerr, Erik Spoelstra top list of highest paid NBA coaches

In 2024, when the Warriors and Steve Kerr agreed to a two-year extension paying him $17.5 million a season, other coaches celebrated — he had driven up the market price overall for coaches.

While other coaches' salaries may have climbed, Kerr remains the highest-paid coach in the league, according to Kurt Badenhausen of Sportico, who did the research on coaching contracts (which are not publicly available). Here are the top 10 highest-paid coaches, all making eight figures a year:

Steve Kerr (Warriors): $17.5 millionErik Spoelstra (Heat): $15 millionTyronn Lue (Clippers): $15 millionRick Carlisle (Pacers): $11 millionIme Udoka (Rockets): $11 millionJoe Mazzulla (Celtics): $11 millionMike Brown (Knicks): $10 millionQuin Snyder (Hawks): $10 millionTaylor Jenkins (Bucks): $10 millionDusty May (Mavericks): $10 million

A few thoughts from the Sportico research:

• Kerr, Spoelstra, and Lue also happen to be the NBA's three longest-tenured head coaches with their current teams.

• Jenkins and May were hired this summer with those eight-figure salaries, with Dallas paying up to get May out of Michigan (where he had just won a national championship). They got hired at higher salaries than established, very successful coaches such as Mark Daigneault in Oklahoma City and Chris Finch in Minnesota.

• The story reports the standard starting salary for an NBA head coach is at least $4 million a season. Two coaches are below that number: Doug Christie in Sacramento, and Micah Nori in Portland, who is on a much-discussed (and despised by other coaches and basketball people) one-year deal with less than $2 million guaranteed, and with options after it. With what Nori has done with the Trail Blazers so far, he deserves a reward of stability (and more cash).

#2575. Match Preview: Liverpool Face Club Brugge Test as Iraola Looks to Restore European Momentum

Following a disappointing defeat against Fenerbahçe in their last Champions League outing, Liverpool return to European action with a trip to Belgium to face Club Brugge.

Andoni Iraola's side will be keen to put that result behind them and get their European campaign back on track. Despite the setback in Turkey, Liverpool have made an encouraging start to the league phase, winning their opening three fixtures before suffering that first defeat.

The Reds will now be looking to respond with a performance that demonstrates the quality and depth available within the squad. With a busy domestic schedule continuing, this is also an opportunity for Iraola to rotate his starting eleven while maintaining the standards expected in Europe.

Club Brugge will provide a difficult test on home soil. The Belgian side are capable of making life uncomfortable for visiting teams, and Liverpool will need to be disciplined, particularly during the opening stages.

I expect Iraola to make changes for this fixture, balancing the need to maintain Liverpool's European momentum with the demands of a busy schedule.

Giorgi Mamardashvili should come into the side, while Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas offer opportunities to rotate the full-back positions. Ronald Araújo and Virgil van Dijk would provide experience and physical presence at the heart of the defence.

In midfield, Trey Nyoni could partner Dominic Szoboszlai, with James McConnell operating further forward as the combative number 10. It would be an interesting selection, particularly given the ongoing questions surrounding Liverpool's midfield balance and the personnel required to make the double pivot work effectively.

The attacking positions could provide opportunities for some of the younger players. Bradley Barcola offers genuine pace and direct running from the right, while Víctor Muñoz could provide a similar threat on the opposite flank. Lewis Koumas would also be given an opportunity to lead the line and demonstrate his ability at senior level.

Nyoni's continued development is another storyline worth watching. The young midfielder has been one of Liverpool's more consistent performers in recent weeks, and another European start would provide further evidence of the trust Iraola is placing in him.

This is a game Liverpool should approach with confidence, but certainly not complacency.

Club Brugge will be determined to make the most of their home advantage, and the Reds should expect a competitive atmosphere and an opponent willing to challenge them physically. Liverpool must be prepared to work hard without the ball and show greater defensive concentration than they did during the defeat in Turkey.

The predicted changes should not mean a drop in ambition. Liverpool have won their opening three Champions League matches and have an opportunity to strengthen their position among the leading sides in the league phase.

For Iraola, this is about more than simply securing three points. It is an opportunity to see how his squad players respond to responsibility, give valuable minutes to emerging talent and maintain competition for places.

The quality is certainly there to win this fixture, but Liverpool will need to be clinical in front of goal and disciplined defensively. I expect an entertaining contest, with Club Brugge capable of causing problems but the Reds ultimately having enough attacking quality to come away with a result.

#2572. Unconventional Racing Rebrands With Pratt Miller And Nielsen For 2027

Entrepreneur Naveen Rao has officially launched Unconventional Racing to unite his North American and European programs under one global brand. The new identity will debut on 10 December at the IMSA-sanctioned test at Daytona International Speedway. This move merges the expertise of Pratt Miller Motorsports in the US with Nielsen Racing in Europe to field cars in LMP2 and LMP3 classes starting in 2027.

Rao aims to build a single entity that operates across both sides of the Atlantic while keeping local operations intact. The team will run an ORECA 07-Gibson LMP2 car in the WeatherTech Championship through Pratt Miller. Before adopting a new identity for the 2027 European Le Mans Series season, Nielsen Racing in Europe will conclude its ongoing Asian Le Mans Series campaign.

The strategy relies on using existing infrastructure rather than building from scratch. Nielsen Racing will provide the personnel and operations for the European endurance program, allowing the team to enter multiple categories immediately without hiring new staff or buying new equipment.

"Unconventional Racing is about building something with genuine international ambition," said Rao, the CEO of Unconventional Racing, according to Sportscar365. He believes this structure lets each program draw on expertise that already exists within the organizations while presenting a unified front to sponsors and fans.

Rao plans to drive in both the ELMS and IMSA LMP2 programs himself. He brings experience from Ferrari Challenge North America and has secured podium finishes in IMSA LMP2 at Watkins Glen and Road Atlanta this past season.

Pratt Miller's partnership represents the American company's third LMP2 season following its 2025 return to prototype racing. This partnership gives Unconventional Racing a strong platform in North American sports car racing. According to reports, Pratt Miller's Director of Motorsport Operations said the move signifies an advancement for the group.

"Pratt Miller Motorsports are very excited to partner with Unconventional Racing working together to build a strong foundation for a global programme," said Maurini, according to DailySportsCar. The collaboration involves sharing engineering and mechanical expertise between the US and European teams to prepare for the 2027 season.

Team Principal Ron Hartvelt joined Nielsen Racing in 2025 and took his current role in March 2026. He will remain with the team as it transitions to the new brand. Hartvelt highlighted that an important Asian Le Mans Series campaign remains to be finished by the team prior to the full rebrand becoming active.

"Unconventional Racing represents an exciting evolution for Nielsen Racing," said Hartvelt. He stressed that the group plans to uphold the Nielsen name's ethos during this new phase while collaborating closely with Pratt Miller staff.

Driver lineups and further details on the North American and European programs will be announced in due course. The team expects to have a clear long-term vision in place as they move toward the 2027 European Le Mans Series and the Michelin Le Mans Cup. Rao's focus remains on creating a stable foundation for global competition.

The new identity reflects growing business opportunities within the sector, aligning the race team with Unconventional AI.

Giddey followed up that epic game with a 2-for-11 performance with 4 points, 11 assists, 2 stocks and 3 turnovers on Monday. He was benched in crunch time (again). If you have Giddey, I'd sell. The game-to-game variance is too erratic.

Heat: Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists with zero turnovers in Sunday's 123-113 win over OKC with Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) out. Miami has won seven straight to reach 10-6. Shout-out to Klay Thompson, who averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 3s over a recent seven-game stretch and is closing in on Ray Allen for third all time in 3s. Keep holding Klay in 12s.

Bucks: Tyler Herro set a new career high in Philly on Saturday, dropping 50 points, then added 32 with 8 assists in Monday's win in Toronto to snap a 13-game skid. At 2-16, start prepping for some shakeups in the rotation — which could impact vets like Herro, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Rookie Brayden Burries (40% rostered) had 14 points, 10 boards, and 4 assists off the bench Monday, and should be rostered in most leagues.

Cavaliers: James Harden dropped 51 in Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games ever (26). Evan Mobley (toe) has missed six straight and is due for re-evaluation this week. Kenny Atkinson has started Tyrese Proctor and Sam Merrill over the past week, but rookie Meleek Thomas (13.3 points in 24 minutes) is still the best streamer here.

Nets: Nolan Traore (right hamstring) will be re-evaluated in 8-10 weeks. Mikel Brown Jr. (19% rostered) got the first crack, starting Monday in Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted: 17 points, a career-high 7 assists and 5 boards in 29 minutes. Egor Demin shot 3-for-13 off the bench. Brown is the add over Demin. The No. 6 pick has a path to 30 minutes a night.

Lakers: Austin Reaves (left heel) practiced fully on Sunday and is targeting a return on Friday in San Antonio. Quentin Grimes averaged 9.2 points through 12 games, then moved into the starting lineup over the last five games, averaging 24.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists. He ranks 31st in 9-cat over that span, with 35.58 fantasy points per game.

Enjoy it now, because he won't see anywhere near 37 minutes a night when Reaves returns. Matisse Thybulle is the keeper. His 39 steals rank second in the league, and he and Wemby are the only players this year with 15+ blocks, 20+ steals and 30+ 3s.

Hawks: Atlanta has won four straight without CJ McCollum, whose left calf strain will be re-evaluated in about four weeks. No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings got next, but don't rush to get him because the Hawks won't play until Friday.

Dyson Daniels, though? He's such a unique fantasy talent. He's posting 9.5 points, 7.4 boards, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals per night. He can't shoot beyond 10 feet, but he's touching nearly every major counting-stats category except blocks and 3s.

Grizzlies: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That hurts. Kris Murray started in his absence on Monday, playing 32 minutes and got 5 stocks. Add him to the watchlist, even though Memphis will likely form a committee between Murray, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (when he gets back). Make sure Cam Spencer (45%) isn't on waivers.

Clippers: Brandon Ingram started in his debut Monday in Houston and posted 16 points, 7 boards, and 4 assists in 27 minutes. The shooting was unsurprisingly rough (6-for-18, 0-for-6 from three), but 18 shots in his first game since May is a great sign. Marc Stein reported that LA is showcasing vets like Rui Hachimura and Kris Dunn before the trade deadline.

Jazz: Svi Mykhailiuk went OFF Sunday for 39 points and 10 threes, both career highs. I'd rather pick up Ace Bailey, though.

76ers: Philly's five-game win streak ended Monday against Portland with Joel Embiid (illness) out. Embiid's been better, and fantasy managers could take the opportunity to float offers because health is always the biggest question mark with Embiid.

Celtics: Four straight losses. Derrick White is shooting 40.1% from the field and 28.8% from 3, well off his 45.4/38.7 peak. I'm holding in 9-cat, but it's been a disappointing start.

Mavericks: Just two games this week, and two scheduled before the NBA Cup next week. Cut fringe Mavs for players who play more games over the next two weeks.

Knicks: Josh Hart is averaging 6.6 points on 34/27/60 shooting. Woof.

Pistons: Over the past five games, Ausar Thompson ranks 16th in 9-cat. He's making 87.5% of his free throws (albeit low volume, but still!)

Magic: Anthony Black continues to lap Jalen Suggs. Suggs is averaging 9-5-4 with 35/29/73 shooting splits. He's down to 73% rostered, but fantasy managers should stay patient as he ramps up from a bone bruise injury that cost him eight games.

Wizards: The Wizards want Trae Young to focus less on scoring and more on passing. Per Kevin O'Connor, Young had 8 minutes of possession time per game over his first 6 games. It's down to 5 minutes over his last 5 games.

Raptors: Toronto lost to the 2-16 Bucks and sits at 6-11 overall. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is shooting at practice but is still a couple of weeks away from returning. Jakob Poeltl is back on the radar after averaging 11.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game in his last three games.

Pacers: At 5-12 without Tyrese Haliburton, Indiana is reportedly looking to make a move. In the meantime, Kelly Oubre Jr. (36%) should be rostered in all leagues.

Hornets: Brandon Miller and Coby White sat all of OT in a four-point loss to the Lakers last week. Minutes restrictions are costing teams Ws.

Timberwolves: Rudy Gobert ranks 114th in points leagues and 290th in 9-cat. His efficiency near the rim is pacing to his worst since his rookie season — he's 17-for-53 on layups through Monday. Plus, his rebounding and block rates are tumbling. Keep an eye on Joan Beringer.

Rockets: At 13-5, Houston owns the NBA's best offensive rating (121.1) and a plus-8.2 net rating (5th in the league).

Nuggets: Nikola Jokić logged triple-double No. 202 on Sunday. He's seven behind Russell Westbrook's record.

Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan is finishing 74% at the rim, up from 66% last season.

Thunder: Nearly 80% of Ajay Mitchell's shots are 2s and he's hitting 28.3% from 3. He'll need to extend that range if the Thunder want to right the ship.

Suns: Four straight wins after Monday's OT victory in New Orleans. If Jalen Green was dropped in a points league, pick him up.

Warriors: Stephen Curry (oblique) is due for re-evaluation this week.

Pelicans: New Orleans sits at 5-14, so it's a team to watch by the deadline. Keep holding the young guys, Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. Everyone else could be on the block.

Kings: Keegan Murray has 12-plus points and seven-plus boards in four of his last five. Rounding into form? Maybe.

#2570. WR Brandon Aiyuk reportedly clears waivers after finally being released by 49ers, would like to sign soon

After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a new team soon.

He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

Aiyuk was subject to waivers, but upon clearing them, he's reportedly a free agent. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that a spot on the Commanders' practice squad is the likeliest next step for Aiyuk.

After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on Nov. 9, at which time the 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption to decide if they wanted to release him, trade him or add him to the 53-man roster. The reinstatement was the first step toward Aiyuk's eventual release.

Aiyuk's breakup with the Niners is no surprise. Leading up to the 2025 season, reports surfaced that guarantees in his contract were voided amid growing frustrations between the organization and the veteran wideout.

Then, in January, 49ers GM John Lynch officially acknowledged the impending divorce between the two sides, stating in his end-of-season news conference, "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers."

Aiyuk is 28 and hasn't played since Week 7 of the 2024 season. Before his injury, he had spent his entire five-year career with the 49ers.

San Francisco drafted him with the 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He had his breakout season in 2022, finishing with 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns. Aiyuk returned in 2023 and improved, finishing with 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

He suffered his injury in 2024 against the Kansas City Chiefs. This kicked off two years of wide receiver injuries for the 49ers.

San Francisco has been playing this season without Aiyuk in consideration for the roster. As such, the Niners have turned to Deebo Samuel, Mike Evans and Keenan Allen in the passing game, with promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling expected to return from injury soon.

If Aiyuk joins Washington, the Commanders will look to get him up to speed as No. 1 wide receiver Terry McLaurin has been ruled out for the season due to a torn ACL. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams have picked up the slack, but Washington could use Aiyuk if he can play close to his pre-injury level.

#2569. Joel Hofer supplants Jordan Binnington as the St. Louis Blues' starting goaltender

Jordan Binnington backstopped the St. Louis Blues to the Stanley Cup in 2019 and Canada to the 4 Nations Face-Off title last year before getting his country to the final at the Olympics in February.

In the NHL, he's now a backup goaltender.

That's because of the emergence of Joel Hofer, who has become the No. 1 guy for the Blues. Hofer ranks second with a .919 save percentage and fifth with a 2.35 goals-against average among goalies who have started at least 15 games.

"He's been awesome the last couple years, and I think people are finally starting to realize how good he is," captain Robert Thomas said. "He's trying to become a starter in the league, and he's got no better mentor than Binner to help him out and push him in the right direction. I think he's showed a lot of maturity this year, and he's only going to get better."

The shift to Hofer, now 26, began last season when he started 43 games to Binnington's 39. That was a tandem approach, and it got St. Louis within reach of a playoff spot before just missing out.

Through the first 24 games this fall, Hofer has started 17 to Binnington's seven. The net is clearly his.

"I'm just trying to go a game at a time and give my team the best chance to win every night," Hofer said. "I'm just trying to have fun doing it. It's a privilege to play in this league and as a goalie to play games in a row. I'm just trying to make the most of it."

Hofer is 10-6-1 for the Blues, who sit in the second and final wild-card spot in the Western Conference with 60 games left to play.

"Joel Hofer's had a great start to the season," coach Jim Montgomery said. "He's just continued what he did from November on last year and just continues to grow in his confidence and asserting himself as a big part of our team."

Binnington also still is — for now. His six-year, $36 million contract signed in 2021 expires at the end of June, and he turns 34 on July 11.

The feisty goalie who earned a reputation for being a big-game performer is a candidate to be dealt before the March 1 trade deadline. For now, Montgomery said Binnington is simply being "an incredible teammate."

"He exudes leadership," Montgomery said. "He is Joel Hofer's biggest supporter, as Hofer is his biggest supporter. And I know that, myself, any time I talk to him, it's an easy conversation and that speaks volumes about him because we're talking about how he's doing and how we're working through things and he's just a consummate professional. He has high-level leadership."

Thomas, who is wearing the "C" for the first time after taking over that role from Brayden Schenn, called Binnington the greatest to play the position in franchise history. Binnington certainly has had his moments to earn that praise, including a 32-save performance to beat Boston in Game 7 of the Cup final in 2019.

Binnington was excellent at the Milan-Cortina Olympics, but his numbers with St. Louis show he is past his prime. Only Chicago's Arvid Soderblom and Vancouver's Kevin Lankinen have a lower save percentage than Binnington's .847 among goalies who have appeared in at least five games.

His teammates still think very highly of Binnington, especially given how he has handled being shuffled into a secondary spot.

"We believe he's one of the best goalies in the league, still," Thomas said. "It's a tough situation for him to be in, but he's a big part of our leadership group and he's really taken that to heart. He's been the ultimate teammate and person. It would be really easy to be frustrated in his situation. He's got a lot of things going on — a contract year, different things — but he's put the team first."

Hofer called Binnington supportive throughout the process of succeeding him.

"I guess this is my fourth year now, so it's been a good journey," Hofer said. "It's been fun with this group. Just trying to build every day. I think we're all going for the same goal here, and when we're all doing that and going in the same direction, it makes things fun."

#2568. Warriors rookie’s meteoric rise comes with glaring defensive concern

The Warriors have turned to rookie Yaxel Lendeborg while Steph Curry is sidelined.

The 24-year-old quickly put together a dominant stretch of games with Curry on the floor, but without the superstar, Golden State has struggled. Evidently, so has Lendeborg and the biggest concern for the No. 11 overall draft pick is on defense.

Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors dribbles during a game against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, in New Orleans. NBAE via Getty Images

ESPN's Zach Kram broke down a glaring concern regarding the rookie's play.

"And the second is his extremely negative on/off data. The Warriors have a 121.0 defensive rating with Lendeborg on the court versus a 99.3 mark when he's off, per Cleaning the Glass. That difference ranks him in the first percentile league wide. Opponents have gotten to the rim way more, committed fewer turnovers and run much more in transition with Lendeborg on the other end."

Golden State Warriors player Yaxel Lendeborg looks on during a game against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio, Texas, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Regardless, Lendeborg is still regarded as a favorite to win Rookie of the Year. The forward has his sights set on another award, though.

Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors plays defense on Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 13, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NBAE via Getty Images

#2566. Sean Payton suspends RB JK Dobbins for Friday's game vs. Steelers due to 'conduct detrimental to the team'

Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters on Tuesday that he is suspending veteran running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Payton said it was due to "conduct detrimental to the team", and the head coach did not elaborate.

Dobbins is in his second season with the Broncos. He began his career with the Baltimore Ravens and then spent the 2024 season with the Los Angeles Chargers before joining Denver last year.

He is currently the team's leading rusher with 324 yards and has added three touchdowns on 99 carries.

The veteran running back played in only 10 games last year, finishing with 772 yards and four touchdowns. Dobbins faced a rookie running back in RJ Harvey last year, and Denver brought in another this year in Jonah Coleman.

Dobbins has said he is happy to do whatever he can to contribute to the team, but last week Coleman had his breakout game with 111 yards and three touchdowns.

#2565. MSU women's basketball edged by Virginia Tech in Emerald Coast Classic final

NICEVILLE, Fla. — Kennedy Blair's career-best scoring game was not enough to help the Michigan State women's basketball team capture the title at the Emerald Coast Classic.

Blair finished with 33 points for the Spartans, who were edged by Virginia Tech, 69-68, in the tournament title game Tuesday, Nov. 24.

Blair helped the Spartans overcome a 13-point second half deficit to take the lead in the fourth quarter. She hit the go-ahead 3-pointer with 1:10 to play to give MSU a 68-65 lead before Virginia Tech scored the final four points. Samyha Suffren hit the game-tying and go-ahead free throws with 4 seconds left to vault Virginia Tech (7-0).

Blair, who opened the Emerald Coast Classic by recording the fourth triple-double in MSU women's basketball history in a Nov. 23 win over Alcorn State, was 11-of-22 from the field and 9-of-11 from the free-throw line in her career-best scoring performance. She was one of two players in double figures scoring for MSU (6-1).

Theryn Hallock contributed 17 points for the Spartans on 7-of-11 shooting from the floor and added seven rebounds.

Suffren led three players in double figures with 19 points to lead Virginia Tech. Leila Wells, a Chelsea native, contributed 10 points for the Hokies.

Week 11 of the NFL season is almost completed with the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) and Washington Commanders (3-5-1) set to play on Monday night.

The week began with Thursday night's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans. The Texans prevailed 26-3 as the Colts performed so poorly offensively that the team decided to move on from quarterback Daniel Jones and released him the next day.

Jones' next destination will be one of the NFL's top stories as Week 11 finishes and the season progresses toward Week 12. The eight-year veteran is expected to clear waivers on Monday and from there, he will wait to see what his best option is, according to ESPN. Among the teams that could line up to sign him are the Arizona Cardinals, New England Patriots and Baltimore Ravens.

The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City to close out Sunday's slate. With the 35-10 victory, the Niners improved to 9-1 to keep hold of the top seed in the NFC. The Buffalo Bills matched them for the NFL's best mark with a 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

One concern for NFL coaches this week might be players celebrating touchdowns with backflips and front-flips. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo and Detroit Lions receiver Jameson Williams each went airborne in their Week 11 games, surely making their head coaches cringe. Teams have seven more weeks to keep their players on the ground.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a new team soon.

He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, according to head coach Sean Payton.

Payton did not get into specifics and told reporters he would not comment further on the situation.

The suspension leaves Denver will be without its leading rusher for Friday's Week 12 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jonah Coleman (302 rushing yards in 6 games) will presumably take over as the starter.

"We'll see how he does," Reid said, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work there, but he'll get out there and move around."

The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo this week for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills.

If there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a big-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

The guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback."

Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

The Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

In the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

If the New England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

While Jones has cleared waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel said he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

The plan is for Sam Darnold to start against the 49ers on Sunday, but Mike Macdonald wants to see the quarterback in practice first before making a final decision.

Darnold has been out for two games due to a quad injury suffered in Week 8.

Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.

They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics said they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants.

"We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play."

Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

After missing nearly a year with tears to his ACL and meniscus, Micah Parsons is set to return to the Packers' defensive line this week. The star linebacker has reportedly been cleared to play as of Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Parsons reportedly needed one final clearance on his knee before getting the green light, and will now make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday.

New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will be sidelined for "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday.

It's still unclear if Newsome will need surgery or if he will land on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games.

"It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh said, via ESPN. "It's going to be multiple weeks."

For more on Newsome's injury, click here.

San Francisco is finally parting ways with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

After a months-long saga around the receiver wanting to be released, Aiyuk was officially waived by the 49ers on Monday. That confirms reports earlier on Monday indicating that Aiyuk would finally be released.

Other teams will have until Wednesday to claim Aiyuk, who will become a free agent after he clears waivers.

Former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was not claimed on Monday, thus making him a free agent.

Jones is free to sign with any team that wants him, and that team can pay him the veteran minimum.

The Colts still owe Jones about $20 million.

The Commanders have activated running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve, and he is off the injury report.

JCM will play Monday night against the Bengals. He hasn't played since Week 5 due to a groin injury.

So far this season, Croskey-Merritt has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries. He also has 40 yards on five receptions.

The Cardinals have reportedly fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Arizona's defense has allowed 355.2 yards per game this season, the seventh-most in the league. The Cardinals' allowing 29.4 points per game is the second-most in the league, trailing only the Raiders at 29.7 points per game.

San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multi-year contract extension with the team, according to reports.

Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the new contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

Exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially announced the agreement. Lynch's current contract was set to expire after this season.

Lynch's new deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will need season-ending surgery on his ankle.

Ferguson is the latest Rams player to be dealing with a long-term injury. Wide receiver Puka Nacua will also miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury. Davante Adams has been sidelined since Week 6, though he is expected back by mid-December.

Ferguson's season ends with him playing in just three games. He finished with 63 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions.

The San Francisco 49ers are reportedly releasing veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to start the year, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings, and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

If the New England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

While Jones waits to clear waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception.

"We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said at his Monday press conference.

"I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there and had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things," he added. "I think that was probably the biggest thing is just saying, 'Hey, getting back into game action. How do you work in the pocket?' These are things that he got so much better on when he got here."

This week, we have to transition right out of Week 11 and right into Week 12, because the NFL week starts on Wednesday due to their increasingly crazy holiday schedule. We have games all week, and because of that, we don't have much time to get prepared for the upcoming fantasy week, so we have to dive right into the deep end.

While we are usually focusing on all the offensive stars around the league, we still have to pay some attention to the defense. IDP fantasy football, which is when you start individual defensive players, is not only a lot more fun, but also a lot more difficult. You have to put a lot more work in than many are willing to, which is why most fantasy owners simply play a team defense.

That's easy enough, and we are here to help you pick the correct defense and special teams to get into your lineups this week. These are our fantasy football D/ST rankings for Week 12.

The Vikings come in as our D/ST1 against Michael Penix Jr. and the Atlanta Falcons. Not only are they the best defense in the league, but we love the matchup against Atlanta.

Penix has not been good, and unless Bijan Robinson can put the whole team on his back, we don't see how the Falcons are going to move the ball in this game. We expect the Falcons to have more turnovers than touchdowns in this game.

New York is a D/ST we are higher on than consensus. We have them three spots above ECR (expert consensus ranking) as our D/ST4 overall, and that is all about the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

That team is falling apart at the seams and outright cut their starting quarterback this week. There is a chance we get the rare big Anthony Richardson game this week, but those games are few and far between. It's far more likely we get the much more common Richardson disaster game.

Miami is another team we are higher on than most. We have them nine spots above ECR as our D/ST14. The Dolphins' defense has been significantly better than most realize, and they have a matchup against the lowly Jets this week. You can use them as a D/ST2 this week.
